title: LacerteHealth bypasses WrapToolHandler and hardcodes sim response
description: LacerteHealth returns a raw string 'reachable (sim)' without using WrapToolHandler.Run and without asking the session manager about mode. The injected _session is unused, the response is identical in sim and live, and a thrown exception would leak as an MCP error instead of a {success:false, statusCode,...} envelope. The TODO comment even concedes the live branch was never wired despite Phase 9 closing.
recommendation: Wrap the body in WrapToolHandler.Run, route through _session for the live HRESULT (e.g. a session.HealthProbe() that returns sim/live identical shape), and return a structured {mode, status} object. Returning a bare string violates Invariant #9 (always structured) and Invariant #2 (the response should be the same shape but should not be a literal sim-only string in live).
rationale: Health is the operator's primary signal that the MCP works. Today it lies in live mode and any internal throw produces an unstructured failure surface.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading HealthTools.cs (lines 25-33), WrapToolHandler.cs, SessionTools.cs (every sibling tool uses WrapToolHandler.Run), LacerteSessionManager.cs (Mode property already exposed, immutable per process), HealthToolsTests.cs, and ARCHITECTURE.md Invariants #2 and #9. The finding is factually accurate: HealthTools is the only tool that bypasses WrapToolHandler, returns a raw string, ignores the injected _session, and literally hardcodes "(sim)" in its output regardless of mode. The slight overreach in the finding: the current body has no code that can throw, so "exception leaks as MCP error" is theoretical not active — but the envelope-shape and mode-honesty arguments are genuine invariant violations. Fix is sim-only and trivial: wrap the body in WrapToolHandler.Run, return { mode = _session.Mode, status = "reachable" }, and update the one existing assertion in HealthToolsTests.cs. No Lacerte SDK or Windows access required. Leaving a live HRESULT probe as a Phase-9 follow-up is fine — the in-session fix is just to stop lying about mode and conform to the envelope contract.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: In-session (sim-only) fix: change LacerteHealth to `Task<string> LacerteHealth() => WrapToolHandler.Run(() => Task.FromResult<object>(new { mode = _session.Mode.ToString().ToLowerInvariant(), status = "reachable" }));` and update the Description attribute to drop the "(sim)" literal. Update HealthToolsTests.LacerteHealth_ReturnsNonEmptyString_InSimMode to assert the JSON envelope contains `"success":true` and `"mode":"simulation"`. Leave the live HRESULT probe (new session.HealthProbe() backed by the bridge) as a Phase-9 follow-up — that part is correctly out of scope until the COM bridge lands. Keep the existing TODO comment but reword to "Phase 9: surface live SDK HRESULT via _session.HealthProbe()" so the shape commitment is already locked in.

title: WriteDetail session chokepoint skips access-map AssertWritable
description: WriteField (line 595) correctly calls FieldAccessMapLoader.AssertWritable before the wire call, but WriteDetail does not. There is no AssertWritable gate anywhere in the detail-write path — only read-only + idempotency are enforced. Boundary Invariant #7 says 'The access map is consulted before every write' with default-refuse on Unknown.
recommendation: Add an AssertWritable equivalent for detail writes (e.g. assertDetailWritable(module, year) gating the whole detail-file write, or a per-field check if the access map ever gains per-detail-column entries). At minimum, add an explicit comment/decision logged in DECISIONS.md noting that detail rows are out-of-scope for the access map, so future readers do not assume Invariant #7 is honored across all writes.
rationale: Detail-file writes can corrupt the per-client store silently (per the DetailsTools doc comment), so leaving the access map disengaged here is the riskiest write path in the system.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading LacerteSessionManager.cs:595 (WriteField calls AssertWritable) vs. 681-752 (WriteDetail does not — only RejectIfReadOnly + idempotency). The access map's shape (module|table|field keyed, where table is a DATA-table number 1-7) genuinely does not model per-client detail-file rows, which have no primary key and no enumerable "field" set — so the original recommendation's "per-field check" option is not actionable without new map design + SDK introspection (Windows-only). However, the literal wording of Boundary Invariant #7 ("consulted before every write") does NOT match actual code, which is a real spec-compliance hole worth closing. CreateClient (line 758+) has the same gap. The actionable, sim-only fix is documentation: scope Invariant #7 in ARCHITECTURE.md to per-field writes and log a DECISIONS.md carve-out explaining detail rows + whole-row CreateClient writes rely on client-side validation (DetailsTools.ValidateDetailWrite) + the SDK's own row-level acceptance rather than the access map. This is useful because the finder's risk concern ("detail-file writes can corrupt the per-client store silently") is real, and a future reader who sees the invariant will reasonably assume the gate is there.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Tighten Invariant #7 in ARCHITECTURE.md to read "consulted before every per-field write (WriteField)" and add a DECISIONS.md entry titled "Detail-row + whole-row writes are outside the access-map gate" that names the two affected paths (LacerteSessionManager.WriteDetail at 681-752 and CreateClient at 758+), explains the map's M|T|F key shape can't address detail rows or whole-row creates, and points readers to the actual safety nets: DetailsTools.ValidateDetailWrite (line ~96, Series/Code/StateAbbr/TSJ shape gates) for details and CreateClient's ClientID length check + SDK-side row validation for creates. Optionally add a one-line code comment in WriteDetail and CreateClient ("// No AssertWritable — see DECISIONS.md 'Detail-row + whole-row writes...'") so the carve-out is visible at the call site. Do NOT invent an assertDetailWritable stub that always returns true; that's worse than silence because it implies a check that isn't there.

title: Live-mode reads throw BridgeUnavailable; sim/live observationally divergent
description: EnsureLive() throws SyntheticStatusCodes.BridgeUnavailable whenever Mode == Live, so every read chokepoint (ListClients, ReadClient, ReadTableCore, ReadDetail, ReadEFStatus) is unreachable in live mode and always returns from the in-memory SimulationStore in sim mode. This violates Invariant #2 (sim and live observationally identical for the happy path) — happy-path live reads cannot succeed at all. The _odbc field is still 'object? = null' (line 60) with the Phase 4 wire-up TODO unfinished, despite the project status claiming all planned tasks done.
recommendation: Either wire the ODBC reader path (LacerteDsnReader) into ListClients/ReadTableCore/etc. behind the Mode == Live branch, or rename EnsureLive() to ThrowIfLive() and document that live reads are a pending sub-stream. The current naming is inverted (EnsureLive throws when live) and confuses readers about the intent.
rationale: Project claims live mode is reachable; the read chokepoints prove otherwise. Either the docs or the code are wrong, and an audit cannot tell which without reading the impl.

verdict.reasoning: The finding is partially correct but misdiagnoses the severity. CONFIRMED: EnsureLive() at lines 880-888 does throw BridgeUnavailable when Mode == Live, and it gates every read chokepoint (ListClients 397, ReadClient 426, ReadTableCore 457, ReadDetail 517, ReadEFStatus 538). The _odbc field at line 60 is still object? = null. CONFIRMED: the name EnsureLive() is semantically inverted — it throws *when* live, so it really means "ensure we are NOT in live mode / proceed only via sim path." REJECTED as a bug/invariant violation: the project documents this explicitly and repeatedly — Todo.md tasks #25, #27, #70, #71, F14 all state live calls throw BridgeUnavailable pending Phase 9; HANDOFF.md line 101 says register/login stub the live call pending Phase 9; REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md line 56 says Phase 9 ships COM bridge as scaffolding only, verifiable only on a Windows + Lacerte box; Todo.md task #88 explicitly defers v0.1.0 tag pending Phase 9 live verification. Invariant #2 ("observationally identical for the happy path") is the *post-Phase-9 target*, not a current claim — currently live mode is scaffolding by design because the dev box has no Lacerte install. The "project claims all planned tasks done" in the task context refers to the in-scope sim work, not the Windows-gated Phase 9 wire-up. So the architectural-bug framing is wrong, but the naming/clarity complaint is real and the fix is genuinely useful and trivially actionable off-Windows.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Rename EnsureLive() to ThrowIfLive() (or EnsureSimPath()) and update the call sites + xmldoc to make the inverted semantics obvious. Add a one-line summary on the method: "Throws BridgeUnavailable in Live mode — every wire chokepoint guards through this until Phase 9 wires the bridge + ODBC reader. Sim path is always reachable." Do NOT attempt the actual ODBC wire-up — that is Phase 4/9 work explicitly gated on Windows + Lacerte SDK and not actionable in this sim-only dev environment. Leave the _odbc TODO and the Phase 9 task #67 references intact.

title: COM instance leak: Writer/Reader never call Marshal.ReleaseComObject
description: Writer.AcquireWriter() and Reader.AcquireReader() Activator.CreateInstance a fresh COM object (LacerteSDK_Access.DBFWriter / .DBFReader) on EVERY wire call, and the wrapping methods (WriteToDBFDatabase, UpdateTaxReturn, WriteDetail, ReadFromDBFData) never release them. In contrast, CanUseNewApisProbe.Probe correctly releases its COM ref in a finally block. On a long-running live session this leaks one RCW per write/read, holding native handles open and bloating the COM apartment until GC eventually finalizes them (which is non-deterministic and can fail under shutdown).
recommendation: Wrap each wire body in a try/finally that calls Marshal.ReleaseComObject(writer)/(reader) — copy the pattern from CanUseNewApisProbe.cs:96-103. Alternatively cache a single Writer/Reader COM instance per process (mirroring LacerteAccessClient._comInstance) and dispose it in Program shutdown. Add a regression test that constructs+disposes N times and asserts handle counts stay bounded (skip on non-Windows).
rationale: Per Boundary Invariant #8 in ARCHITECTURE.md, COM lifetimes are owned at the bridge layer. CanUseNewApisProbe demonstrates the project already knows to release; Writer/Reader inconsistently don't. In live mode this is a silent leak that only manifests after hundreds of writes on a Windows + Lacerte box — exactly the kind of bug that escapes off-Windows test runs.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading the files. Writer.cs (lines 40, 76, 115) and Reader.cs (line 37) all call AcquireWriter/AcquireReader (which does Activator.CreateInstance on the COM ProgID at lines 175 and 88 respectively) inside a try/catch that has NO finally block releasing the RCW. The project has two established patterns for COM release that this code violates: (1) CanUseNewApisProbe.cs:96-103 does the per-call try/finally + Marshal.ReleaseComObject pattern, and (2) LacerteAccessClient.cs:302-313 caches a single instance and releases in Dispose. The leak is real on live Windows: every write/read allocates a new RCW that lingers until the next GC finalizer pass. The fix is a textbook copy-paste of the CanUseNewApisProbe pattern into four spots, requires no Windows or Lacerte SDK install, and the existing off-Windows tests (WriterTests/ReaderTests) will continue to pass because AcquireWriter still throws BridgeUnavailable before any COM allocation off-Windows. Minor caveat: the audit's citation of "Boundary Invariant #8" is wrong — #8 in ARCHITECTURE.md is about Intuit auth ticket lifetimes, not COM — but the technical finding is independently sound.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Apply the CanUseNewApisProbe.cs:96-103 pattern to all four COM call sites (Writer.WriteToDBFDatabase, Writer.UpdateTaxReturn, Writer.WriteDetail, Reader.ReadFromDBFData). Concretely: pull `var writer = AcquireWriter(...)` out of the try, then wrap the existing try/catch in an outer try/finally whose finally does `if (writer != null) { try { Marshal.ReleaseComObject(writer); } catch { /* best-effort */ } }`. Do NOT take the cached-instance route the audit mentions as an alternative — Writer/Reader are static classes with no disposal hook, and threading a singleton through Program shutdown would change lifecycle semantics for marginal gain over per-call release. Skip the suggested handle-count regression test: it requires Windows + a real COM ProgID to be meaningful (the off-Windows path short-circuits at AcquireWriter before any RCW exists), so it would be a no-op skipped test that adds noise. Instead, add a one-line comment at each release site pointing to CanUseNewApisProbe as the canonical pattern, and note the manual handle-count check in REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md under "Manual Live-Mode Verification".

title: Idempotency cache has TOCTOU race; duplicate side-effects possible
description: TryReplayIdempotent and StoreIdempotent are unsynchronized. Two concurrent calls with the same idempotencyKey + same payload both miss the cache (TryGetValue returns false), both execute the wire call (write to ODBC/COM), both call StoreIdempotent. The result: the underlying SDK write happens TWICE despite the operator passing the same idempotency key — the exact bug idempotency keys are meant to prevent. Per agent 07 §9 the cache state machine is supposed to be atomic.
recommendation: Use ConcurrentDictionary<string, Lazy<Task<IdempotencyCacheEntry>>> keyed by idempotencyKey, OR wrap the read-execute-write triple in a per-key lock (a tiny ConcurrentDictionary<string, object> of lock tokens). The first inflight call materializes the Lazy/Task; concurrent callers await the same task. Add a stress test that fires N concurrent WriteField calls with the same key and asserts only ONE underlying SimulateFieldWrite was invoked.
rationale: Idempotency is one of the named boundary invariants (DECISIONS.md / agent 07). A 9102 IdempotencyConflict is documented for divergent payloads, but the more dangerous case — concurrent identical replays causing duplicate writes — is currently unguarded. With MCP tools potentially driven by a model that retries on stdio jitter, this race is reachable in normal operation.

verdict.reasoning: The race is real as described. LacerteSessionManager.cs lines 1129-1156 confirm: `_idempotencyCache` is a `ConcurrentDictionary` (line 89), but `TryReplayIdempotent` (`TryGetValue`) and `StoreIdempotent` (indexer set) are separate operations with the wire call between them (e.g. lines 589-673 for WriteField, 692-750 for WriteDetail, 769-835 for CreateClient). Two concurrent calls with the same key both see the cache miss, both execute, both store — duplicate write to ODBC/COM. The existing tests (LacerteSessionManagerTests lines 283-310) cover sequential happy-path and conflict-payload, but never concurrent. Agent 07 §9 (docs/research/agents/07-qb-mcp-patterns.md) does name idempotency as a state machine, even if "atomic" is the finder's gloss; the QB reference is single-threaded JS so they sidestepped it. Severity is debatable — stdio MCP requests are typically serialized by the client and this is a single-operator tool (CLAUDE.md: "Personal tool"), so concurrent same-key collisions are unlikely in normal use. But the boundary invariant ("sim+live observationally identical", idempotency contract) is real, the fix is small (~20 lines + one xUnit test), and the fix is fully sim-actionable off-Windows. The finding stands as a worthwhile hardening; the agent's severity:"high" overstates real-world risk for this single-operator tool (medium is more honest), but the fix-vs-cost ratio is excellent.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Replace the unsynchronized `TryReplayIdempotent`/`StoreIdempotent` pair with per-key serialization. Concrete approach: add `private readonly ConcurrentDictionary<string, SemaphoreSlim> _idempotencyLocks = new();` Refactor the three write paths (WriteField line 589/673, WriteDetail line 692/750, CreateClient line 769/835) to call a single helper `Task<T> ExecuteIdempotentAsync<T>(string? key, string payload, Func<Task<T>> body)` that (1) returns body() directly if key is null, (2) acquires `_idempotencyLocks.GetOrAdd(key, _ => new SemaphoreSlim(1,1))`, (3) inside the critical section re-checks the cache, runs body if miss, stores result on success, (4) releases the semaphore in finally. Do NOT remove the semaphore from the dictionary on release (cheap to leak; removing introduces a separate race) — accept O(unique-keys) memory or add a periodic compaction tied to session lifetime. Add one sim-only xUnit test in `LacerteSessionManagerTests` that uses `Task.WhenAll` to fire N=20 concurrent WriteDetail calls with the same idempotencyKey + identical payload, then asserts `ReadDetail("1001").Count` only grew by 1 (mirroring the existing replay test's observable signal at line 291-295). Downgrade the finder's stated severity from "high" to "medium" in the changelog — this is hardening of a named invariant, not an observed live bug, on a single-operator tool with serialized stdio transport.

title: No CI workflow — build/test only run locally
description: No .github/workflows/, azure-pipelines.yml, or .gitlab-ci.yml exists. The project has 481 passing tests, two-mode (sim vs live) discipline that explicitly enables off-Windows verification, and a hard regression checklist — yet there is no automated build that exercises that promise on every change. README claims 'sim mode runs anywhere,' but nothing enforces that the sim build stays green on a Linux/Mac runner. The CLAUDE.md operating system mentions handing off across many contractor-like sessions; CI is the cheapest enforcement mechanism for the boundary invariants.

title: WireLog opens + closes log file on every record (per-call FS open)
description: WriteRecord calls File.AppendAllText(path, line + Environment.NewLine, Encoding.UTF8) inside the lock for every wire op. That is an open/seek-to-end/write/flush/close cycle per record. With LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1, every read tool (Odbc.Query, ListClients, ReadClient, ReadTable, ReadEFStatus, etc.) AND every write tool emits at least one record, often two (the WireLog wraps the outer chokepoint AND Odbc.Query inside it). Order-of-magnitude estimate: a single LacerteClientList against 5k clients triggers ~1 record; a tight tool loop over 1000 reads = 1000 open/close pairs serialized through _writeLock. Concatenating with `line + Environment.NewLine` also allocates a fresh string per write.
recommendation: Keep a long-lived StreamWriter (FileStream opened with FileMode.Append, FileShare.Read, AutoFlush=true) per UTC date, rolling at midnight; write line + '\n' via WriteLine to avoid the concat allocation. Continue holding _writeLock around WriteLine to preserve thread-safety. Dispose on AppDomain.CurrentDomain.ProcessExit. Falls back to current behavior on IOException so a transient lock doesn't poison the next write.
rationale: Per-op file open is the textbook hot-path I/O anti-pattern the audit brief called out. With the log behind an env flag the impact is bounded to debug sessions, but those are exactly when the operator is hammering the server diagnosing a problem — the worst time to make every call ~5-10x slower.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading src/LacertMCP.Server/Logging/WireLog.cs lines 211-223: WriteRecord does call File.AppendAllText inside _writeLock for every record, which is an open/seek-to-end/write/flush/close syscall cycle per wire op. The finding is real, not a misread. With LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1 every Record/RecordSync call hits this path, and the codebase nests WireLog around tool chokepoints AND around inner Odbc.Query calls, so the per-call cost is doubled in the read path. Actionability is high — it's a pure C# change in an already-tested file with EnableForTests/DisableForTests/WriteForTest hooks, no Windows/Lacerte SDK needed. Usefulness is real-but-bounded: the log is default-off, but the audit's point is correct that debug mode is exactly when an operator least wants a 5-10x latency tax. Worth fixing.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Replace the per-call File.AppendAllText with a cached StreamWriter keyed by full log file path (path includes UTC date, so a new path naturally appears at midnight rollover — no separate timer needed). Sketch: a static Dictionary<string, StreamWriter> guarded by _writeLock; on each WriteRecord, compute the target path, look up the writer, and if absent (new date or first call) close+remove any stale entries for a different path then open `new StreamWriter(new FileStream(path, FileMode.Append, FileAccess.Write, FileShare.Read), Encoding.UTF8) { AutoFlush = true }` and cache it; call `writer.WriteLine(line)` (avoids the `line + Environment.NewLine` concat AND avoids per-write encoding allocations). Keep the outer try/catch swallowing IOException as today, but on catch null out the cached writer for that path so the next call re-opens cleanly (this also covers transient AV/lock churn on Windows). Register an AppDomain.CurrentDomain.ProcessExit handler that takes _writeLock, flushes+disposes all cached writers, then clears the dict. Update DisableForTests to flush+dispose any cached writer whose path is under the test's logDir so temp-dir cleanup doesn't fail with sharing violations — alternatively, since the test surface already calls WriteForTest with arbitrary dirs, expose an internal FlushAndCloseForTests() and call it from DisableForTests. Validate by adding a test that calls WriteForTest 1000x against a temp dir and asserts only one file handle is opened (observable via the existing AppendAllText catch + a counter) and that DisableForTests releases the handle before the temp dir is deleted.

title: Idempotency cache has no eviction, TTL, or size cap
description: _idempotencyCache is a ConcurrentDictionary<string, IdempotencyCacheEntry> that grows monotonically. StoreIdempotent unconditionally writes for every WriteField/WriteDetail/CreateClient that supplies an idempotencyKey, retaining the SHA-256 fingerprint, the boxed result object (CreateClientResult for CreateClient — contains a string ClientNumber, but for WriteField it's a boxed int), and CreatedAt. There is no scrubber, no max-size, no TTL eviction loop, and the IdempotencyCacheEntry record carries CreatedAt only for diagnostics. A 24-hour operator session that writes 10k fields with idempotency keys (a realistic e-file prep workload — every field on every state return) accumulates 10k entries with no path to release them short of process restart.
recommendation: Add a sliding-window TTL (e.g. 24h to match the auth window, per agent 07 §9) and a hard max-entry cap (e.g. 10k) with LRU eviction. Simplest: convert to MemoryCache<string, IdempotencyCacheEntry> from System.Runtime.Caching (net48 ships it) with AbsoluteExpiration = DateTimeOffset.UtcNow.AddHours(24) on Set, and SizeLimit. Alternatively, run a single-shot Timer that walks _idempotencyCache once per hour and TryRemove entries where CreatedAt is older than the threshold. Update agent 07 §9 in DECISIONS.md to document the chosen eviction policy.
rationale: Long-running personal-tool servers commonly stay up for days. Unbounded caches keyed on caller-supplied strings are also a low-grade DoS vector if any tool path lets the LLM influence the key without bound.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly in LacerteSessionManager.cs (lines 89-90, 1129-1156) and IdempotencyCacheEntry.cs. The cache is a plain ConcurrentDictionary with no TTL, no size cap, and no scrubber; CreatedAt is recorded but never consulted. StoreIdempotent is called from three write paths (WriteField, WriteDetail, CreateClient) and writes unconditionally. The auth-window framing is also correct — the 24h Intuit re-registration window is the documented session boundary (research agent 02 §3,5), so keys from a prior auth window are semantically stale anyway. Severity 'high' is overstated for a single-operator personal tool (realistic write volume per session is dozens-to-hundreds of fields, not 10k), but the underlying defect — unbounded cache with caller-influenced keys and no eviction — is real and worth fixing. Pure in-process data-structure change, exercisable in sim, no Windows or SDK dependency. Confidence high.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Keep the ConcurrentDictionary (no new package reference). Make CreatedAt earn its keep: (1) in TryReplayIdempotent, if entry.CreatedAt < UtcNow - 24h, TryRemove it and treat as miss; (2) in StoreIdempotent, after writing, if _idempotencyCache.Count > IdempotencyCacheMaxEntries (const = 10_000), scan and TryRemove all entries older than the TTL, and if still over cap, remove the oldest N by CreatedAt. Both paths are lazy/opportunistic — no Timer, no background thread, no race-prone scrubber. Expose TTL + MaxEntries as private const fields so a future test can shorten TTL for verification. Add tests: (a) expired entry on TryReplay returns miss + re-executes, (b) over-cap StoreIdempotent prunes oldest entries, (c) replay-with-same-payload within TTL still hits. Add a DECISIONS.md entry (not agent 07 §9 — that's research notes, not project decisions) documenting the 24h-matches-auth-window choice and the 10k cap as a DoS guardrail.

title: ListClients pulls full roster then paginates in-tool (no SQL TOP/OFFSET)
description: LacerteClientList calls _session.ListClients(nameFilter, int.MaxValue) — explicitly defeating any server-side cap — then hands the materialized list to Pagination.Page which slices in memory. Pagination.Page (line 38-71) takes the source IEnumerable and immediately .ToList()s it to compute total. The corresponding live ODBC template at SqlTemplates.cs line 57 is `select * from [DATA1-Client Info]` with no TOP/OFFSET clause; in live mode this means every paginated request round-trips the entire DATA1 table over ODBC. Realistic DATA1 sizes for a small practice are 2-5k clients; large practices push 50k+. For limit=100 the operator pays the full 50k cost per request.
recommendation: Push limit/offset down to SQL. The Lacerte ODBC driver supports `SELECT TOP n` and per agent 03 §4 also supports basic `WHERE`. Add an offset-aware template (e.g. `SELECT TOP {limit} * FROM [DATA1-Client Info] WHERE C1_0 > '{lastSeenCursor}'`) or a row_number wrapper. In the sim path, change ListClients(filter, limit) to honor a paged cursor and only materialize the slice. As a cheap interim, stop passing int.MaxValue from the tool and pass `offset + limit` to the session so the materialization cost is bounded.
rationale: Brief explicitly called this out (pagination: O(n) vs SQL TOP/OFFSET). Audit shows both the tool layer AND the SQL templates skip the push-down.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed against source. ClientsTools.cs:32 literally passes int.MaxValue to _session.ListClients, defeating the session-side Take(limit) bound. Pagination.cs:43 does `source.ToList()` to compute total — so in sim, the entire DBF dict gets cloned (CloneRow) per request before slicing. SqlTemplates.cs:57 is `select * from [DATA1-Client Info]` with no TOP/WHERE — when live ODBC wires up against this template, every paged request will full-scan DATA1. This is the same O(n) anti-pattern the brief flagged. The fix is genuinely in-scope for sim: changing the tool to pass `offset + limit` is a one-line bounded-materialization win; adding a `Data1Top(int n)` SQL template is pure string-template code with no Lacerte dependency, and a unit test can assert the rendered SQL contains `TOP n`. The cursor-based variant in the original recommendation is shakier (C1_0 is alphanumeric ClientNumber, not guaranteed monotonic for cursor semantics), so I'd drop that and stick with TOP + offset+limit. Not bikeshedding — total throws away the bounded-Take, and the SQL template lock-in is a live-mode footgun being introduced now while it's cheap to fix.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Two-part sim-only fix, both verifiable off-Windows: (1) In ClientsTools.LacerteClientList, replace `int.MaxValue` with `offset + Math.Min(limit, Pagination.MaxLimit)` so the session materializes at most one page-worth of rows (Pagination.Page still computes correct `total` because we pass it the same bounded slice — actually no: total would be wrong. So instead, push limit/offset into LacerteSessionManager.ListClients itself: add overload `ListClients(filter, limit, offset)` that returns `(rows, total)` where total is computed from the filtered IEnumerable via `.Count()` on the dict (O(n) but no clone) and rows is the bounded `.Skip(offset).Take(limit).Select(CloneRow).ToList()`. Update the tool to consume that and bypass Pagination.Page entirely, or have Pagination.Page accept a pre-counted total. (2) In SqlTemplates, add `Data1Top(int n)` returning `select top {n} * from [DATA1-Client Info]` and `Data1TopWhereName(...)` for name-prefix; unit-test the rendered SQL. Leave the unbounded `Data1All` constant alone for callers that legitimately need the full roster (schema dump). Skip the cursor-based WHERE C1_0 variant — ClientNumber sortability isn't guaranteed and offset+TOP is the safer first step.

title: CLI quick-start claim `doctor exit 1 off-Windows; that's expected` is wrong
description: Quick-start says `& lacerte-mcp.exe doctor   # exit 1 off-Windows; that's expected`. Per `DoctorCommand.Run` the off-Windows contract is exit 2 (PARTIAL — skipped probes, no reds) — exit 1 only fires when a probe genuinely fails. The README later (line 91) and the DoctorCommand XML doc correctly describe the 0/1/2 contract, so the quick-start line directly contradicts the documented contract.
recommendation: Change to `# exit 2 off-Windows (partial — skipped probes); exit 0 fully green; exit 1 means a real failure`. Add a sentence noting that exit 1 on a fresh install is expected because the AppID probe fails until `register` runs.
rationale: Contradictory exit-code docs cause CI authors and operators to write the wrong shell guards (`if doctor; then ...` vs `case $? in`).

verdict.reasoning: Verified against DoctorCommand.cs (lines 17-19, 84-103): the documented contract is exit 0 (all green), exit 1 (any Fail), exit 2 (any Skipped, no Fails). Off-Windows, probes 1, 3, 4, 5 are Skipped, probe 2 (x64) Passes on x64, probe 6 (LACERTE_DATA_PATH) Warns or Passes, probe 7 (AppID) Fails only if no AppID is persisted. So off-Windows you actually get exit 2 in the steady-state (AppID persisted from prior `register` or sim test) and exit 1 only on a fresh checkout where AppID is missing — which is itself a Fail, not "expected because off-Windows." The README quick-start line on 28 conflates the two and contradicts both the same file's line 91 and the DoctorCommand XML doc. A README edit is fully in-session — no Lacerte/SDK install needed.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Replace line 28 with two lines that match the actual 0/1/2 contract and call out the fresh-checkout case explicitly: `& src/LacertMCP.Cli/bin/x64/Debug/lacerte-mcp.exe doctor   # exit 2 off-Windows = PARTIAL (Windows-only probes skipped); exit 1 = a probe failed (e.g. fresh checkout with no AppID — run 'lacerte-mcp register' or test fixture seeds it); exit 0 = all green (Windows + Lacerte install).` Optionally also fix the `& lacerte-mcp.exe` form referenced in the finding's `description` field (the actual line uses the longer `src/.../lacerte-mcp.exe` path — same fix applies). No other docs need changing: line 91 and the DoctorCommand XML doc are already correct.

title: WireLog redaction regex misses common PII fields (DOB, address, phone, email, names)
description: The redaction regex covers only SSN, EIN, BankAccountNumber, RoutingNumber. Tax returns contain plenty of other PII that flows through Write/Detail/CreateClient paths and gets logged verbatim when LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1: TaxpayerSSN/SpouseSSN/DependentSSN (different key names than the bare 'SSN'), EmployerEIN/FedEIN, DateOfBirth/DOB/BirthDate, FirstName/LastName, EmailID/email, PhoneNumber, Address1/StreetAddress, City/State/Zip. CreateClient logs first/last/email verbatim (LacerteSessionManager.cs:789-790). WriteDetail logs the whole row including Description (often free-form taxpayer notes). The Lacerte field naming convention is uppercase or PascalCase and varies by table — a bare 'SSN' rarely appears as a JSON key in practice; the SDK fields look like 'TaxpayerSSN'/'C1_15'/etc.
recommendation: Expand the regex alternation to cover TaxpayerSSN|SpouseSSN|DependentSSN|FederalID|FedEIN|EmployerEIN|DateOfBirth|DOB|BirthDate|EmailID|HomePhone|WorkPhone|CellPhone|Address[12]?|StreetAddress|ZipCode and the conventional Lacerte numeric field codes that hold these (e.g. C1_14, C1_15, C1_19 on DATA1-Individual — list in spec). Better: switch from a key-name allowlist to a key-name DENYlist that redacts anything not in a small set of explicitly-safe keys (op, ts, durationMs, statusCode, module, table, year, dryRun, hasMore, count). Add a unit test asserting a CreateClient/WriteDetail wire log line contains no raw email/DOB substring.
rationale: WireLog is the operator's auditing surface. The current redaction list is the *minimum* the spec called out and is far short of what a tax-software wire log actually surfaces. A debug log on disk that contains taxpayer SSNs (under a non-bare key) or DOBs is a meaningful breach exposure for a tool that handles tax returns.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading src/LacertMCP.Server/Logging/WireLog.cs (regex at line 62-64 only covers SSN|EIN|BankAccountNumber|RoutingNumber) and the three callers that pass PII verbatim: (1) CreateClient at LacerteSessionManager.cs:789 logs `new { args, dryRun }` where CreateClientArgs (line 1224-1229) is a record with FirstName/LastName/EmailID — none redacted; (2) WriteDetail at line 700 logs `new { clientNumber, row, replaceIndex, dryRun }` where DetailRow contains a free-form `Description` field; (3) WriteField at line 601 logs `new { table, clientNumber, field, value, ... }` — the secret is keyed by the literal `"value"` with the SSN-bearing field name (e.g. C1_15) in the sibling `"field"` slot, so the current key-name regex CANNOT match this exposure at all, regardless of how many alt-names are added. The finding is real and the auditing surface is a meaningful breach exposure for a tax-software tool. Purely a Logging/redaction change + unit tests — fully implementable off-Windows with the existing WireLog.Redact public API and the existing test harness pattern (WireLogTests.cs).
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Three-part fix, all in WireLog.cs + WireLogTests.cs (no Windows/SDK dependency):

1) Expand the key-name regex alternation to cover Lacerte-realistic PII keys: SSN|TaxpayerSSN|SpouseSSN|DependentSSN|TIN|ITIN|PTIN|EIN|EmployerEIN|FederalID|FedEIN|BankAccountNumber|RoutingNumber|DateOfBirth|DOB|BirthDate|EmailID|Email|HomePhone|WorkPhone|CellPhone|PhoneNumber|FirstName|LastName|MiddleName|Address1|Address2|StreetAddress|City|ZipCode|Zip|Description.

2) Add a second pass that specifically targets the WriteField pattern `"field":"<name>","value":"<secret>"` (the field codes that hold PII like C1_15/C1_19 won't appear as JSON keys — they appear as the *value* of a `"field"` key). Match `"field"\s*:\s*"(?:<known-pii-codes>)"\s*,\s*"value"\s*:\s*<json-literal>` and redact the value. List PII field codes via a small static set sourced from `Lacerte_MCP_Structure_Spec.md` (the spec already lists them per DATA1 module).

3) Add the missing unit tests in WireLogTests.cs asserting that (a) a CreateClient-shaped record `{"args":{"FirstName":"Jane","LastName":"Doe","EmailID":"j@e.com"}}` produces no raw "Jane"/"Doe"/"j@e.com" substring; (b) a WriteDetail-shaped record with a Description containing "SSN 111-22-3333" gets the Description value blanked; (c) a WriteField-shaped record `{"field":"C1_15","value":"111-22-3333"}` redacts the value. The existing redaction test pattern at line 19-53 is the template.

Defer the full key-name DENYlist refactor — the regex approach stays viable for now and is a smaller blast radius than restructuring WriteRecord's serializer.

title: Tool error context dict bypasses WireLog redaction — PII echoed to MCP client
description: WrapToolHandler.SerializeError serializes the LacerteSDKError.Context dictionary straight to the MCP wire with no redaction. Tools and the session manager routinely put potentially-sensitive caller input into context: clientID, dataPath (absolute filesystem path), field, value (the actual field value being written), taxType, args (full CreateClientArgs including FirstName/LastName/EmailID — see LacerteSessionManager.cs:778, CreateClientTools.cs:191), exception messages from late-bound COM (Registration.cs:104 puts ex.Message into context — could include taxpayer data the SDK echoed back). WireLog redaction only runs on the disk log path; the on-wire MCP error envelope is unredacted.
recommendation: Apply the same redaction pass to SerializeError's output JSON (and to the entire envelope, not just context). Better: scrub Context at the point of LacerteSDKError construction so callers can't accidentally leak — add a helper LacerteSDKError.WithSafeContext(IDictionary, allowedKeys) that drops everything not in an allowlist. At minimum strip 'value', 'args', 'rawError', 'firstName/lastName/emailID', and any key whose value looks like an SSN/EIN/DOB before serializing.
rationale: An MCP client (an LLM) has fewer authentication boundaries than a disk log — sending PII back over the wire potentially exposes it to model providers, transcripts, and any tool the LLM forwards to. The error path is exercised constantly (every read-only rejection, every access-map miss) so the leak surface is large.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed in code: WrapToolHandler.SerializeError (src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/WrapToolHandler.cs:72-85) serializes err.Context directly into the MCP wire envelope, and WireLog.Redact() is only invoked from WriteRecord on the disk-log path — never from the tool error path. The leak surface is real: DetailsTools.cs:146/158/172 put validated user input under a 'value' key, the generic-Exception wrapper at line 64 puts ex.Message into context.rawError, and Registration.cs:104/Bridge paths put ex.Message into context.reason — any of those messages could echo taxpayer data the SDK returned. The success path is also unredacted, which means SSN/EIN values returned from ODBC reads also bypass redaction on the wire — actually a larger hole than the audit flags. The finding does overstate two items: CreateClientTools.cs:191 only puts clientID+taxType into context (not the full CreateClientArgs), and LacerteSessionManager.cs:778 only puts clientID — args is only logged via WireLog where redaction applies. Net: real issue, narrower than claimed but still worth fixing. Fully actionable off-Windows since WireLog.Redact is already public, the fix is a single-file change, and it's unit-testable in sim.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Single-file fix in src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/WrapToolHandler.cs: apply the existing WireLog.Redact() pass to the serialized JSON in BOTH SerializeError (line 84) and the success path (line 51) — `return WireLog.Redact(JsonSerializer.Serialize(envelope, JsonOptions));`. This reuses the project's proven SSN/EIN/BankAccountNumber/RoutingNumber regex and closes the wire-vs-disk asymmetry symmetrically (success envelopes also carry ODBC-read row data with those fields). Add an additional regex hit for 'rawError' and 'reason' keys so COM-echoed taxpayer data in exception messages gets scrubbed too — extend WireLog._redactRegex's key alternation to include those two keys, or add a second regex constant in WrapToolHandler. Skip the allowlist refactor for now (LacerteSDKError.WithSafeContext) — it's a bigger change that breaks ~25 throw-sites; revisit only if redaction-by-regex proves leaky. Add 3 unit tests: (a) field-write rejection where value='123-45-6789' SSN-shaped is redacted, (b) generic-exception wrap where ex.Message contains 'SSN: 123-45-6789' is redacted, (c) success envelope reading a row with an SSN column is redacted.

title: Hoist _moduleFileName + _moduleTaxTypes onto Modules so 3 copies become 1
description: The Char->filename basename map ('I'->"individual", etc.) is duplicated verbatim in 3 places (FieldAccessMapLoader, MetadataTools, FieldAccessCommand). FieldAccessCommand.cs:26-28 even contains a comment acknowledging the duplication. Separately, the Char->TaxType[] accept-list ('I'->["Individual","1040"], etc.) is duplicated between SimulationStore and CreateClientTools.
recommendation: Add FileBasename and AcceptedTaxTypes properties to Schema/Modules.ModuleInfo (or two static helpers Modules.FileBasenameFor(char) / Modules.AcceptedTaxTypesFor(char)), then delete the 3+2 private copies. Tests in Schema/ already exercise Modules; the single-source invariant comes for free.
rationale: Adding the 10th module would require editing 5 files in sync today; in the natural design it's a single row in Modules.All. This is the highest-impact simplification in the audit.

verdict.reasoning: Verified verbatim: the Char->filename basename dictionary is copy-pasted in three places (FieldAccessMapLoader.cs:61-72, MetadataTools.cs:30-41, FieldAccessCommand.cs:29-40 — the last with an in-code apology comment), and the Char->TaxType[] accept-list is duplicated between SimulationStore.cs:265-277 and CreateClientTools.cs:39-51 (also with an apology comment). Modules.cs is the obvious home: it already enumerates the same 9 modules as a sealed-record catalog with thorough test coverage in ModulesTests.cs. The refactor is pure C# in Schema/ + 4 call sites — no Windows, no live SDK, no COM/ODBC touch. It also closes a real correctness risk: the sim+live observational-identity invariant in ARCHITECTURE.md depends on SimulationStore and CreateClientTools agreeing on accepted TaxType aliases, which today is enforced by copy-paste. Adding a 10th module (or fixing an alias typo) currently requires 5 coordinated edits; after the refactor it's one row in Modules.All.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Extend Schema/Modules.cs as the single source. Add two fields to ModuleInfo: `string FileBasename` and `IReadOnlyList<string> TaxTypeAliases`. Populate them in the existing Modules.All initializer (the 9 rows become e.g. `new ModuleInfo('I', "Individual", "Individual", "individual", new[] { "Individual", "1040" })`). Add two convenience helpers — `Modules.FileBasenameFor(char) -> string?` and `Modules.AcceptsTaxType(char, string) -> bool` (case-insensitive, matching the existing semantics) — so call sites don't have to chase the record. Then delete the 5 private dictionaries and replace lookups: FieldAccessMapLoader.LoadModule uses `Modules.GetByChar(m)?.FileBasename`; MetadataTools validates via `Modules.GetByChar(module) != null` and uses `.Name` for the moduleName field instead of the basename (small UX bonus — "Individual" reads better than "individual" in tool output); FieldAccessCommand uses the same; SimulationStore + CreateClientTools call `Modules.AcceptsTaxType`. Extend ModulesTests.cs with two table-driven tests (FileBasename matches existing values; TaxTypeAliases case-insensitive accept). One commit, ~80 lines net delete, all 481 tests should stay green.

title: EF status SQL template omits EFilingId/EFId/InstanceId that tool returns
description: EFileTools.LacerteEfStatus [Description] promises `flat rows with EFilingId, ClientId, EFId, InstanceId, Status, StatusDate.` The simulation path in LacerteSessionManager.ReadEFStatus() returns exactly those 6 keys. But the live SQL template `EfStatusJoin` selects only `ci.C1_0, ci.C1_2, ci.C1_3, s.EFStatus, s.EFStatusDate` — missing `ef.Id AS EFilingId`, `ef.EFId`, `ef.InstanceId`. Spec §2 documents the shape: `EFilings (Id, ClientId, EFId, InstanceId)` and `EFStatuses (EFilingId, EFStatus, EFStatusDate)`. When live mode lands, sim and live will return different column sets — a direct violation of the Two-mode parity invariant (CLAUDE.md `Simulation and live must be observationally identical for the happy path`). Also note: the doc-comment claims `Latest EF status per client` but there is no MAX(StatusDate) / row-number filter, so the JOIN actually returns full status history.
recommendation: Rewrite EfStatusJoin to: `select ci.C1_0 as ClientId, ef.Id as EFilingId, ef.EFId, ef.InstanceId, s.EFStatus as Status, s.EFStatusDate as StatusDate from [DATA1-Client Info] as ci left outer join [EFilings] as ef on ci.C1_0 = ef.ClientId left outer join [EFStatuses] as s on ef.Id = s.EFilingId` so the live shape matches the sim shape and the tool description. Either rename the constant or add a separate `EfStatusLatest` query if `latest per client` is also needed.
rationale: Direct violation of the two-mode parity invariant once live wires up + tool description promises columns the SQL does not return.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly. `SqlTemplates.EfStatusJoin` (SqlTemplates.cs:159-163) selects `ci.C1_0, ci.C1_2, ci.C1_3, s.EFStatus, s.EFStatusDate` (5 cols, copied verbatim from docs/research/agents/03-odbc-dbf-access.md:223). But `LacerteSessionManager.ReadEFStatus()` (LacerteSessionManager.cs:541-551) returns 6 keys: `EFilingId, ClientId, EFId, InstanceId, Status, StatusDate`, and the tool `[Description]` on EFileTools.cs:22 explicitly promises those 6. The parity test `ReadEFStatus_ReturnsRowsWithEfilingId` only runs against the sim path, so it cannot catch the divergence — the moment live mode wires up, the same MCP tool would return a totally different column set (and would not contain `EFilingId`, the very key the test checks). This is a clean violation of the CLAUDE.md "Simulation and live must be observationally identical for the happy path" invariant. Fix is a pure string edit in a const and is sim-only-friendly. Bonus auxiliary issue the finder caught is also real: the doc-comment says "Latest EF status per client" but no MAX/window filter exists in the SQL or the sim — both return full history.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Rewrite `SqlTemplates.EfStatusJoin` so the SELECT list matches the sim contract exactly: `select ci.C1_0 as ClientId, ef.Id as EFilingId, ef.EFId, ef.InstanceId, s.EFStatus as Status, s.EFStatusDate as StatusDate from [DATA1-Client Info] as ci left outer join [EFilings] as ef on ci.C1_0 = ef.ClientId left outer join [EFStatuses] as s on ef.Id = s.EFilingId`. Also fix the misleading XML doc-comment from "Latest EF status per client" to "All EF status rows joined per client (full history)" — neither sim nor SQL filters to latest, so the comment is just wrong. Then add a column-shape assertion to `SqlTemplatesTests.EfStatusJoin_*` (e.g., `Assert.Contains("EFilingId", ...); Assert.Contains("EFId", ...); Assert.Contains("InstanceId", ...);`) so the parity contract is locked at the template level and will fail loudly if the SELECT list drifts again. No live wire-up required for any of this.

title: Pre-TY21 WriteToDBFDatabase row-number path uses int.Parse(clientNumber) placeholder
description: Spec §4 Write: `lacerte_field_write — pre-TY21: WriteToDBFDatabase(appId, dataPath, dbf, rowNum, field, value).` The session manager's WriteField, when CanUseNewApis returns false (TY18-TY20), calls `_bridge.WriteField(appId, ctx.DataPath, ctx.Year, ctx.Module, table, rowNum, field, value)` with `int rowNum = int.TryParse(clientNumber, out var rn) ? rn : -1`. The comment acknowledges: `the field-write tool layer (Phase 6 task #51) replaces this with the real lookup` — but no lookup exists. ClientNumber strings are typically alphanumeric (e.g. `JOHNS`, `SMITH`); int.TryParse will return false and pass `rowNum = -1` to the SDK, which the live SDK will reject with OutOfIndex (4) or a DBnError. Pre-TY21 writes are effectively broken for any non-numeric ClientID.
recommendation: Implement a ClientNumber → row-number lookup before the WriteToDBFDatabase call. The cheapest path is an ODBC `select ROWNUM, C{t}_0 from [DATA{t}-...]` over the active module table, cached per (datapath, year, module, table) — invalidated on writes to that table. Alternatively, surface the row-number lookup as a precondition tool (`lacerte_resolve_row(table, clientNumber)`) and require operators to pass rowNum explicitly. Without a lookup, the documented pre-TY21 path cannot work on real data.
rationale: Spec mandates rowNum keying for pre-TY21; current implementation guarantees rowNum=-1 for typical ClientIDs, making the TY18-TY20 write path non-functional once live wires up.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading LacerteSessionManager.cs:645 and SqlTemplates.cs:28-30. ClientNumber in this codebase is documented and validated as a 1-8 char uppercase alphanumeric identifier (e.g. JOHNS) — the same string used throughout REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md, tests, and the spec. int.TryParse("JOHNS", ...) returns false, so the live pre-TY21 path will always call WriteToDBFDatabase(..., rowNum: -1, ...) for the canonical test client. The code's own comment (lines 638-644) admits this is a placeholder awaiting "the field-write tool layer (Phase 6 task #51)" to inject a real lookup, but FieldWriteTools.cs (the task #51 deliverable) does no such lookup — it just plumbs args through to WriteField. So the documented pre-TY21 write path is non-functional once live wires up. The fix is actionable off-Windows: add a Bridge.ResolveRowNumber(table, clientNumber) method, implement it for sim (trivial — the ConcurrentDictionary is already keyed by ClientNumber, so iterate to find the ordinal position or back it with an OrderedDictionary), and stub the live implementation as an ODBC `select ROWNUM from [...] where C{t}_0 = ?` (the ODBC reader path already exists; only the live ODBC execution needs Windows verification, identical to every other live wire call in the project). Sim tests can fully exercise the new lookup; live verification slots into REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md alongside the existing Writer.WriteToDBFDatabase TY20 check on line 72. Severity is correctly "high" — this is one of three documented write entrypoints in the spec.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add `int ResolveRowNumber(string appId, string dataPath, int year, char module, int table, string clientNumber)` to ILacerteBridge. Sim implementation enumerates the table's ConcurrentDictionary (Clients/Statuses/Displays — DATA1/5/6 are keyed by ClientNumber alone; DATA2/3/4 need extra keys but spec §4 pre-TY21 row-keyed writes only target the C{t}_0 row, so resolution is well-defined) and returns the 1-based ordinal. Live implementation issues `select ROWNUM from [DATA{t}-...] where C{t}_0 = ?` over the ODBC connection pool (the connection plumbing already exists in src/LacertMCP.Server/Odbc/ConnectionPool.cs). In LacerteSessionManager.WriteField at line 645, replace the int.TryParse fallback with `int rowNum = _bridge.ResolveRowNumber(appId, ctx.DataPath, ctx.Year, ctx.Module, table, clientNumber); if (rowNum <= 0) throw new LacerteSDKError(StatusCodes.OutOfIndex, ...);`. Cache the (datapath, year, module, table, clientNumber) → rowNum result on the session and invalidate on writes to that table. Add a REGRESSION_CHECKLIST.md entry under Manual Live-Mode Verification to confirm row-number resolution against JOHNS / TY20 Individual matches the value used in the existing line-72 check. The ODBC `select ROWNUM` step requires live verification (same as every other live wire path) but the sim path, the cache, the invalidation, the error surface, and the wireup are all testable in-session and close the actual spec gap.

title: AutoReconnect: 2 of 4 whitelisted HRESULTs untested; ExternalException path untested
description: AutoReconnect.TransientHResults whitelists 4 HRESULTs (0x800706BA, 0x80010108, 0x8001010A, 0x80010001 — AutoReconnect.cs:43-46) but tests only exercise the first two (RpcUnavailable + RpcDisconnected, AutoReconnectTests.cs:101-113). RPC_E_SERVERCALL_RETRYLATER (0x8001010A) and RPC_E_CALL_CANCELED (0x80010001) — both common during Lacerte's COM message-filter contention — have zero coverage. The ExternalException fallback (AutoReconnect.cs:148) and the bare-Exception ex.HResult branch (line 155) also have no test, so a marshaled COM error that arrives non-typed will silently miss retry without anyone noticing.
recommendation: Add [Theory] cases covering all 4 HRESULTs in IsTransient (parameterize the existing RpcUnavailable test). Add one IsTransient test that throws a raw ExternalException with each whitelist code, and one that throws a base Exception with HResult set to 0x8001010A. These are 6 tiny fact methods and they pin down the resilience contract the operator depends on for live-mode flake tolerance.
rationale: Resilience is the load-bearing live-mode feature — a regression that drops a whitelist entry would be invisible. AutoReconnect is wrapped around every live wire call (LacerteSessionManager.cs:198, 631, 647, 732, 813); any silent miss costs real operator time.

verdict.reasoning: Verified the finding by reading both files. AutoReconnect.cs:41-47 declares 4 transient HRESULTs in the whitelist; AutoReconnectTests.cs only tests 0x800706BA (line 104) and 0x80010108 (line 111). The two untested HRESULTs (0x8001010A RPC_E_SERVERCALL_RETRYLATER and 0x80010001 RPC_E_CALL_CANCELED) are precisely the ones tied to COM message-filter contention — a real Lacerte concern. The ExternalException branch (AutoReconnect.cs:148-151) and the bare ex.HResult fallback (lines 155-158) are also genuinely untested — a developer could delete either branch without any test failing. Per CLAUDE.md, "simulation and live must be observationally identical for the happy path" and resilience is wrapped around every live wire call, so silently dropping a whitelist entry or branch would erode the operator-facing flake tolerance with no signal. The fix is pure unit-test work in the sim test project (Xunit, no Lacerte/Windows needed), trivial to land in-session. The recommendation is already tight and concrete; I refined it slightly to specify converting the existing per-HRESULT facts into a single [Theory] for the IsTransient happy path, plus dedicated facts for the ExternalException and base-Exception fallback branches so a regression deleting either fallback fails loudly.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Replace IsTransient_RpcUnavailable_True and IsTransient_RpcDisconnected_True with one [Theory] over all 4 whitelisted HRESULTs (0x800706BA, 0x80010108, 0x8001010A, 0x80010001) using COMException. Add: (1) [Theory] IsTransient_ExternalException_TrueForAllWhitelisted — constructs a System.Runtime.InteropServices.ExternalException with each HRESULT and asserts true (pins the AutoReconnect.cs:148-151 branch); (2) [Fact] IsTransient_BaseException_HResultFallback_True — creates new Exception("x") { HResult = unchecked((int)0x8001010A) } and asserts true (pins the AutoReconnect.cs:155-158 branch); (3) [Fact] IsTransient_BaseException_NonWhitelistedHResult_False (negative control). Keep the existing E_FAIL negative test. ~6 small test methods, all sim-only, no Windows dependency. Mirror the same theory in WithRetrySync if a separate test class exists.

title: FieldAccessMapLoader overlay precedence + 3 of 5 AssertWritable branches untested
description: FieldAccessMapLoader.AssertWritable (FieldAccessMapLoader.cs:121-163) emits 5 distinct status codes — ExposedForRead, NotExposed (Hidden+NotExposed), FieldNotSupported (overlay), UnknownFieldAccess, and the defensive Error default. Tests cover only ExposedForRead + UnknownFieldAccess. The Hidden→NotExposed(7), NotExposed→NotExposed(7), and NotSupported→FieldNotSupported(26) branches have no test asserting the right statusCode. Worse: the overlay-wins-over-base lookup order (FieldAccessMapLoader.cs:89-93) — the cornerstone of TY21 deltas — has zero coverage. FieldAccessMapCoverageTests.cs:160 only validates the overlay JSON parses; nothing proves an overlay entry actually shadows a base entry, nor that a malformed overlay JSON doesn't poison the cache (the catch-free LoadOverlay at line 191-214 will throw and propagate on bad JSON).
recommendation: Seed the static caches via ResetCacheForTests + reflection (the existing WireLogSessionIntegrationTests.cs:42 pattern) to inject a Hidden / NotSupported / overlay-shadowing-base entry, then assert AssertWritable throws StatusCodes.NotExposed (7) / FieldNotSupported (26). Add one test that writes a malformed overlay JSON to a temp Schema dir and asserts the loader degrades gracefully (today it throws JsonException through LoadOverlay).
rationale: The access map IS the write-safety boundary per ARCHITECTURE.md Invariant: 'access map consulted on every write'. Three of its enforced outcomes ship untested — a regression in the switch ordering would let a Hidden field through with the wrong code (or no code). Overlay precedence is the entire mechanism for TY21-specific deprecations; untested means a TY21 overlay landing could silently fail to mask a deprecated field.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading FieldAccessMapLoader.cs and the two test files. title: Universal C{t}_0 ReadOnly rule is case-sensitive; lowercase fields bypass it
description: `if (field == "C" + table.ToString() + "_0") return FieldAccess.ReadOnly;` is an ordinal case-sensitive equality. A caller passing `"c1_0"` (lowercase) skips the universal ReadOnly rule. The fallthrough then looks up `"I|1|c1_0"` in the base map (also case-sensitive, populated with uppercase keys) — miss — returns Unknown. So a write to lowercase `c1_0` would be blocked by the Unknown gate (9012, force:true overridable!) rather than by the unconditional ReadOnly gate. This violates the ARCHITECTURE.md invariant that the universal rule applies to every module/table.
recommendation: Use case-insensitive comparison: `if (string.Equals(field, "C" + table + "_0", StringComparison.OrdinalIgnoreCase))`. Apply the same fix to the access-map lookup key construction (build the key with normalized case, or load the dict with StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase). Add a regression test that lowercase/mixed-case C{t}_0 still returns ReadOnly.
rationale: Boundary invariants must be unconditional. A field name that round-trips through JSON or a model-generated payload can easily come back lowercase; the operator-facing 9012 (with the friendly `force:true` escape hatch) would let an LLM force-override a write to a primary-key field — exactly the failure mode the universal rule was designed to prevent.

The fallthrough builds the lookup key `"I|1|c1_0"` (line 86) and queries a `Dictionary<string, FieldEntry>` deserialized from JSON with the default case-sensitive `StringComparer`, so uppercase-keyed entries miss too. `AssertWritable` (line 150-156) then returns `Unknown`, which `force:true` callers can override (line 151) — exactly the soft gate the universal rule was supposed to harden. The base JSON files are currently empty stubs, but the bypass is structural and will bite the moment the maps are populated or an LLM emits a lowercase field name. Fix is pure in-process C# (no Lacerte/Windows needed), and existing tests in FieldAccessMapLoaderTests.cs make a regression test trivial. Marked high confidence — read the code and the round-trip is exactly as described.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Normalize the field name once at the top of `GetFieldAccess` rather than scattering `StringComparison` arguments. Concretely, after the null guard on line 81: `var normField = field.ToUpperInvariant();` and use `normField` for the universal-rule comparison and the key construction. This guarantees the universal rule and base/overlay lookups stay consistent without needing to also re-key the deserialized dictionaries (which would otherwise require a post-deserialize copy into a `Dictionary<string, FieldEntry>(StringComparer.OrdinalIgnoreCase)` for both base and overlay loaders). Add three regression tests to FieldAccessMapLoaderTests.cs: (1) `GetFieldAccess('I', 1, "c1_0", 2024)` returns `ReadOnly`; (2) `AssertWritable('I', 1, "c1_0", 2024, force: true)` still throws `ExposedForRead`; (3) mixed-case `"C1_0"` vs `"c1_0"` parity. Also worth confirming the field-write tool layer isn't already uppercasing — grep showed no normalization in FieldWriteTools.cs or WriteField, so the loader is the right place to fix it.

title: Pre-TY21 row-number lookup uses int.Parse(clientNumber) with silent -1 fallback

title: TaxYearOverlay loaded per-year only; deltas don't propagate to later years
description: LoadOverlay reads `ty{yy}-not-supported.json` for exactly the requested year. The semantically-named `ty21-not-supported.json` reads as 'fields not supported starting in TY21', but the loader only consults it when year == 2021. A WriteField for TY22, TY23, or TY24 falls back to the base map and would incorrectly allow writes to fields that were dropped in TY21. There's no mechanism to layer overlays cumulatively (e.g. apply ty21 + ty22 + ty23 overlays when year == 2024).
recommendation: Define the overlay semantics explicitly in DECISIONS.md: either (a) each overlay is full-replace for that year only (current behavior — rename files to make this clear), or (b) overlays are cumulative deltas from the previous year. If (b), have LoadOverlay walk overlays from a baseline year up to the requested year and merge them (later overlays win on conflict). Add tests that pin the chosen semantic.
rationale: The shards are empty today, so this is latent — but once schema introspection populates ty21-not-supported.json (follow-up F5), TY22-25 writes will silently bypass the gate that TY21 enforces. Spec compliance for the access-map invariant fails open instead of failing closed.

verdict.reasoning: The finder's read of the code is correct — `LoadOverlay` reads exactly `ty{yy}-not-supported.json` for the requested year only, never the prior years. However, the finder misframes this as a bug. Agent 04 §6 (the authoritative research at C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/docs/research/agents/04-field-access-map.md, lines 158–186) explicitly designs this as per-exact-year, full-replace: "Overlays are keyed by exact taxYear. A TY22 entry does not inherit from TY21 — each year's 'not supported' list is shipped explicitly." The filename `ty21-not-supported.json` follows the spec wording (Lacerte_MCP_Structure_Spec.md line 74) — it's the "Not Supported Fields in TY21" list, meaning fields not supported in the TY21 build, not "dropped starting TY21." So this is documented design, not a bug. BUT the finder is right that (a) the semantic is buried in research notes rather than DECISIONS.md, (b) the naming is genuinely ambiguous and invites the misread that just happened, (c) there is no test pinning the per-year semantic (the only overlay test just asserts the file parses), and (d) the latent failure mode is real once F5 populates ty21 — someone must remember to populate ty22/ty23/ty24 too or writes silently fail-open against dropped fields. Fix is doc + tests, fully sim-only, in-session actionable.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: The semantic is already decided (per-exact-year, full-replace, per Agent 04 §6) — don't change behavior, harden it: (1) Add a dated entry to DECISIONS.md citing Agent 04 §6: "Per-year overlay files are full-replace, not cumulative deltas. Each TY ships its own complete `tyNN-not-supported.json` listing every field dropped in that build, even if previously dropped." (2) Update the XML doc on `LoadOverlay` and the header on `Schema/FieldAccessMap/README.md` to state this explicitly; reword the README's "Overlays only store deltas" line (currently misleading — it implies deltas from base, but reads to a casual eye as deltas from prior year). (3) Add a coverage test in FieldAccessMapCoverageTests that pins the semantic: seed ty21 overlay with a NotSupported entry, assert GetFieldAccess(...,2021) returns NotSupported AND GetFieldAccess(...,2022) returns the base map value (i.e. no inheritance). Use a temp Schema dir + ResetCacheForTests to avoid polluting real shards. (4) Add a manifest-driven sanity check: if `manifest.json#overlays` lists `ty21-not-supported` but not `ty22-not-supported` and the build year is ≥ 2022, log a warning at loader init (or fail the existing manifest test) — this catches the real failure mode the finder is worried about (forgetting to ship a year). title: BuildPayload SHA-256 + JsonSerializer runs on every write even when idempotencyKey is null
description: WriteField, WriteDetail, and CreateClient ALL compute payload = BuildPayload(...) before calling TryReplayIdempotent, regardless of whether idempotencyKey was supplied. BuildPayload at line 1158 serializes the (op, args[]) tuple via JsonSerializer.Serialize(canon) (default options — no cached instance) then SHA256.Create + ComputeHash + Convert.ToBase64String. TryReplayIdempotent then short-circuits at line 1132 when key is null, throwing the just-computed hash away. StoreIdempotent at line 1153 does the same null check. So on the common case (no idempotency key) every write pays the full serialize+hash+base64 cost for nothing. SHA256.Create also allocates a fresh hash provider per call rather than using a cached instance.
recommendation: Hoist the `if (string.IsNullOrEmpty(idempotencyKey))` check ABOVE the BuildPayload call so the payload is only computed when actually needed. Also cache a static JsonSerializerOptions on BuildPayload and switch from SHA256.Create() to SHA256.HashData(bytes) (or a static ThreadLocal<SHA256> on net48 where HashData isn't available). This eliminates a per-write JSON pass + 32-byte hash allocation + base64 encoding for the dominant code path.
rationale: Brief flagged JsonSerializerOptions caching. The bigger win here is just not doing the work at all in the no-key path — which is most writes outside e-file retry loops.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at the cited lines. WriteField (586-588), WriteDetail (691-695), and CreateClient (768) all call BuildPayload unconditionally, then TryReplayIdempotent at line 1132 short-circuits when key is null/empty — throwing away a freshly computed JsonSerializer.Serialize + SHA256.Create + ComputeHash + Convert.ToBase64String. StoreIdempotent at line 1153 also no-ops on null key. So in the common no-idempotency-key path the entire serialize+hash+base64 cost is pure waste. Fix is a localized refactor in a single file with no live-mode dependency, easily covered by existing tests (the 481-test suite already exercises these write paths). Useful because writes are on the hot path and the wasted work includes a per-call SHA256 allocation plus a Dictionary allocation plus a UTF-8 byte buffer plus a base64 string — all for nothing. Not bikeshedding.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Two-part fix in LacerteSessionManager.cs: (1) In WriteField (~line 586), WriteDetail (~691), and CreateClient (~768), guard the BuildPayload call: `string payload = string.IsNullOrEmpty(idempotencyKey) ? string.Empty : BuildPayload("WriteField", ...)`. The existing TryReplayIdempotent + StoreIdempotent already no-op on null/empty key, so the empty payload is never inspected. (2) In BuildPayload (line 1158), hoist a `private static readonly JsonSerializerOptions s_payloadJsonOptions = new JsonSerializerOptions();` to avoid the default-options allocation per call. Skip the SHA256.HashData suggestion — it's .NET 5+ and not available on net48; once the hoist lands, BuildPayload runs only on explicit idempotency-key writes (e-file retries etc.) where the SHA256.Create cost is irrelevant. Do not introduce a ThreadLocal<SHA256> — adds complexity for a now-cold path. Existing idempotency tests in LacertMCP.Tests should cover this without modification; add one assertion that confirms BuildPayload is bypassed when key is null (or just observe via a counter in debug).

title: SimSnapshot deep-clones full active module per dry-run write
description: SimSnapshot walks Clients, SubClients, States, StateSubs, Statuses, Displays, Forms, AND Details for the active module and CloneDbfRow's every row, then SimRestore replays the entire snapshot back into the live module by Clear+repopulate. For a single-field dry-run write on a module with 5k clients × (1 DATA1 + ~3 subclients + ~5 states + ~10 forms + ~50 detail rows), that is ~300k CloneDbfRow / dictionary inserts per dry-run write. Detail rows are NOT actually cloned — line 1073 does `kv.Value.ToList()` which makes a shallow copy of the list but shares the DetailRow instances (DetailRow is an immutable record, so OK for now, but the asymmetry will bite the moment DetailRow gains a mutable member).
recommendation: Replace whole-module snapshot with per-operation undo records. WriteField touches exactly one (table, key) → snapshot only the prior value of that one Fields[field] entry, then on restore re-set/remove it. WriteDetail appends one row OR replaces at replaceIndex → snapshot just the prior row at that index. CreateClient assigns a new ClientNumber → snapshot just NextClientNumber and remove the added Clients entry. This drops the cost from O(module) to O(1) per dry-run write while keeping the same external contract. The brief flagged this directly ("Snapshot/Restore: full deep-clone cost — can it be incremental?").
rationale: Dry-run is meant to be a cheap preflight; today it's the most expensive write path. With realistic module sizes a single dry-run can take tens of milliseconds where the real write takes microseconds — inverting the cost relationship.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/LacerteSessionManager.cs:1054-1098. SimSnapshot performs a deep clone of every entry in Clients/SubClients/States/StateSubs/Statuses/Displays/Forms via CloneDbfRow on every dry-run write, and SimRestore replays the full snapshot via Clear+repopulate. The Details list is shallow-copied (kv.Value.ToList()), but DetailRow is a sealed record (SimulationStore.cs:46-57) of strings + double?, so the asymmetry is currently safe — though it is a latent footgun the moment DetailRow gains a mutable member. The three call sites (lines 656, 739, 824) each mutate a tiny, well-defined slice: WriteField touches exactly one Fields[field] entry on one row; WriteDetail appends one row or replaces at one index; CreateClient bumps NextClientNumber and adds one Clients entry. Incremental undo is straightforward C# in-memory work with no Windows/Lacerte dependency. The file even carries a TODO at lines 1032-1035 acknowledging the current implementation is a placeholder ("a per-call deep clone of only the active module is enough... for now"), so this is a known shortcut, not a misread. Fix is actionable in-session, materially improves the dry-run cost curve, and removes a latent DetailRow mutability hazard. Not bikeshedding given the stated dry-run-as-cheap-preflight contract.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Replace SimSnapshot/SimRestore with per-operation undo closures returned from a small helper. Concretely: (a) WriteField — capture `(table, key, field, hadPrior, priorValue)` before `row.Fields[field] = value`; restore by setting back or removing. Validation throws (SubClientIDRequired/StateAbbrevRequired/OutOfIndex) happen before any mutation, so the dry-run wrapper should only register an undo *after* ApplySimFieldWrite has located the row and is about to write — making failed dry-runs free. (b) WriteDetail — capture `replaceIndex.HasValue ? (clientNumber, replaceIndex.Value, priorRow) : (clientNumber, appendedIndex=list.Count)` under the same `lock (list)` that performs the mutation; restore reverses inside the same lock. (c) CreateClient — capture `(priorNextClientNumber, assignedKey)`; restore decrements NextClientNumber via Interlocked.Exchange and TryRemove's the Clients entry. Shape the dry-run wrapper as `try { Apply...; } finally { undo?.Invoke(); }` with `Apply...` overloads returning an `Action?` undo (null when nothing was mutated, e.g. validation threw). This drops dry-run cost from O(module) to O(1), eliminates the DetailRow shallow-copy hazard, and keeps the external contract identical. Keep the existing SimSnapshot/SimRestore types around for the planned Stream A task #23 (transactional batched ops) — that use case actually wants the whole-module clone, so don't delete it, just stop using it for single-op dry-runs. Add a perf test that does ~1000 dry-run WriteFields against a Seed module to lock in the improvement and guard against regressions.
