title: dataPath connection-string injection: '}' and other ODBC delimiters not handled
description: Build wraps dataPath in braces only if it contains ';'. The brace form does NOT escape an embedded '}' — to embed a literal '}' inside an ODBC brace-quoted value the convention is to double it ('}}'). A dataPath like 'C:\foo}bar;DSN=Other' (or even 'C:\foo}; Driver={OtherDriver}') would terminate the brace early and let an attacker inject arbitrary connection-string keys (potentially pointing at a different ODBC driver, enabling file-based attack surfaces). Also missing: '=' inside the value (some providers interpret), null bytes, CR/LF. Even though dataPath today flows from the operator's lacerte_set_context call (so the threat model is mostly defensive), the function is a reusable boundary helper and an LLM could be prompted to pass a malicious dataPath.
recommendation: Always brace-wrap the dataPath and double any embedded '}' inside it: var safe = '{' + dataPath.Replace("}", "}}") + '}'. Reject dataPaths containing control chars (< 0x20) or null bytes outright with ArgumentException. Add unit tests for dataPaths containing ';', '}', '{', '=', and CR/LF.
rationale: Connection-string injection is a known class — ODBC parsers honor brace-escape quirks identically across providers. The bracing-only-when-semicolon optimization saves nothing meaningful and creates an unnecessary parser-confusion surface.

verdict.reasoning: Verified in src/LacertMCP.Server/Odbc/ConnectionStringBuilder.cs lines 58-65: the code conditionally wraps dataPath in braces only when a ';' is present and never escapes embedded '}'. Per the documented .NET ODBC/OLE DB connection-string grammar, the literal '}' escape inside a brace-quoted value is '}}'. A dataPath like 'C:\\foo}; Driver={OtherDriver}' would break out and inject a second Driver key. The threat model is non-trivial: dataPath flows in from the LLM-callable lacerte_set_context tool (src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/SessionTools.cs line 70), so a prompt-injected operator session could supply a hostile value. The helper is currently only referenced from tests — production wiring is imminent (Phase: live ODBC reader), which makes this the cheapest moment to harden it. Fix is pure string handling + xUnit tests, fully doable off-Windows; existing test at line 49-51 will need its assertion updated since the recommended fix always brace-wraps.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: In src/LacertMCP.Server/Odbc/ConnectionStringBuilder.cs Build(): (1) Reject upfront with ArgumentException if dataPath contains any control char (c < 0x20, including '\0', '\r', '\n', '\t') — these have no place in a filesystem path and are the highest-risk parser-confusion characters. (2) Always brace-wrap dataPath unconditionally and double any embedded '}': var safe = "{" + dataPath.Replace("}", "}}") + "}". Drop the IndexOf(';') branch entirely — the conditional bracing saves nothing and creates the parser-confusion surface. (3) Update the existing test Build_Returns_Exact_Driver_Datapath_ReturnType_TaxYear_Shape (line 12-16) and Build_Driver_Name_Is_Always_Brace_Wrapped (line 54-58) to expect the now-always-braced Datapath form. Add new Theory tests for dataPaths containing '}', '{', '=', '}}', leading/trailing whitespace inside braces, and reject-tests for '\0', '\r', '\n'. (4) Add an XML-doc remark on Build() noting the brace-wrap-always policy so future maintainers don't re-introduce the heuristic. No need to touch '=' handling beyond bracing — brace-quoted values handle '=' fine per the ODBC grammar.

title: dataPath path-traversal / write-outside-expected-root not validated
description: LacerteSetContext accepts any string as dataPath and forwards it to SetContext, where the only validation is IsNullOrWhiteSpace. The dataPath is then passed verbatim to the ODBC driver (which opens DBF files), and to the live bridge for COM writes. There is no validation that dataPath is an absolute path, that it resolves under an expected root (e.g. C:\Lacerte or LACERTE_DATA_ROOT), that it doesn't contain '..' traversal, or that it points to a directory that actually looks like a Lacerte data folder (presence of DATA1*.DBF). An LLM prompted by an attacker could SetContext to '\\evil-host\share' (UNC) or 'C:\Windows\System32' and trigger arbitrary file probes via the next ODBC read. Same issue with LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH — WireLog.ResolveConfig (Logging/WireLog.cs:234-238) trusts the env var verbatim and will create directories anywhere the process can write.
recommendation: In SetContext: require Path.IsPathFullyQualified(dataPath) (or the net48 equivalent — check for ':\\' / '/' prefix + reject ':' in subsequent chars beyond drive letter), reject embedded '..', reject UNC (starts with '\\') unless an explicit LACERTE_ALLOW_UNC=1 escape hatch is set, optionally enforce that the resolved path is under LACERTE_DATA_ROOT when that env var is set. For LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH: resolve to a canonical path and confirm it's under the user's profile or a small allowlist of roots.
rationale: A tax-return MCP server has elevated read/write privileges on the operator's machine. Any 'set this path' tool that an LLM can call is an arbitrary-file-access primitive unless explicitly gated.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading the cited code. SessionTools.LacerteSetContext (lines 69-96) only checks module length; LacerteSessionManager.SetContext (lines 307-340) only checks IsNullOrWhiteSpace, year floor, and module membership — no path validation. The dataPath then flows verbatim into bridge.UpdateTaxReturn/WriteField/WriteDetail (lines 632/648/733) and into sim store keying. WireLog.ResolveConfig (lines 234-238) trusts LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH verbatim and later Directory.CreateDirectory(cfg.LogDir) at line 215 will create arbitrary directories. The threat model — an LLM-callable 'set this path' tool with elevated filesystem reach on a tax-return server — is sound, not bikeshedding. Fully sim-actionable: this is pure C# path-string validation (Path.GetFullPath, UNC prefix check, '..' detection, root allowlist) that needs no Lacerte SDK or Windows-only APIs; existing SessionToolsTests already drives SetContext and DiscoverDatapaths with a temp-tree pattern so new validation tests slot in. Confidence high on the SetContext gap; the WireLog gap is real but lower impact since env-var control usually implies operator scope.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Land a new PathValidation.ValidateDataPath helper in src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/ and call it from LacerteSessionManager.SetContext immediately after the existing IsNullOrWhiteSpace check. Rules: (1) Path.GetFullPath inside try/catch to canonicalize and catch malformed input; (2) reject if Path.IsPathRooted is false; (3) reject any input where the original string contains '..' as a path segment (Regex on separator-bounded '..'); (4) reject UNC (starts with '\\\\' or '//') unless LACERTE_ALLOW_UNC=1; (5) when LACERTE_DATA_ROOT is set, require canonical path to be under it via case-insensitive StartsWith with trailing-sep normalization. Throw LacerteSDKError with a new SyntheticStatusCodes.InvalidDataPath so the structured-error invariant holds. For WireLog.ResolveConfig: canonicalize LACERTE_DEBUG_LOG_PATH via Path.GetFullPath, reject UNC unless gated, and require result to live under %USERPROFILE%, %TEMP%, or %LACERTE_DATA_ROOT%; on rejection silently fall back to ./logs (don't throw — existing comment at WireLog.cs:220-221 says logging must never break the operator path). Add tests in SessionToolsTests covering UNC reject, '..' reject, relative-path reject, allowlist pass, and both env escape hatches. Touch: src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/SessionTools.cs, src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/LacerteSessionManager.cs, src/LacertMCP.Server/Logging/WireLog.cs, src/LacertMCP.Server/Errors/SyntheticStatusCodes.cs (new code), src/LacertMCP.Tests/Tools/SessionToolsTests.cs.

title: Late-bound COM dynamic dispatch invokes methods with caller-controlled arguments unchecked
description: Writer.UpdateTaxReturn and Writer.WriteDetail pass operator-supplied field/value/series/description/etc. straight to a dynamic COM dispatch (w.UpdateTaxReturn(...) and w.WriteToDetailFile(...)). The COM marshaller will faithfully convert any object the caller supplies — string, Int32, Double, IDispatch — but the SDK's COM methods historically perform their own buffer concatenation on the value before writing to DBF. A value containing embedded null bytes, control characters, or unexpectedly large strings could corrupt the DBF row (the SDK does NOT validate detail-row shape per the comment in LacerteSessionManager.cs:679). DetailsTools validates Series/Code/StateAbbr/TSJ but does NOT bound the length of Prefix, Suffix, Source, ImportSrc, Description, nor the value parameter on field writes.
recommendation: In DetailsTools.ValidateDetailWrite, add max-length checks on every string field (look up SDK column widths in the field-access map; common cap is 50-255 chars). In FieldWriteTools.LacerteFieldWrite and UpdateReturnTools, reject value when value is a string and contains control chars (\x00-\x1F except \t/\n) or exceeds a reasonable cap. Reject value when its CLR type is not one of the expected primitives (string/int/long/double/decimal/bool/DateTime/null) — currently 'object?' accepts arbitrary JSON shapes.
rationale: The COM SDK is documented as not validating row shape; the MCP server is the last line of defense before the DBF gets a corrupt row that silently breaks a tax return. A null byte in a Description field is the kind of bug an LLM will produce by accident and the operator won't notice until the return won't e-file.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed against the cited code. Writer.cs lines 80-82 and 125-129 pass operator-controlled strings (field, value, Prefix, Suffix, Source, CityAbbr, ImportSrc, Description) directly into a `dynamic w` COM dispatch with no length, content, or type checks. DetailsTools.ValidateDetailWrite (lines 126-177) only validates series/code/stateAbbr/tsj — five other detail-row strings are pass-through. FieldWriteTools declares `value` as `object?` advertising "scalar — string, number, or boolean" but never enforces it; an array or object JSON literal would deserialize as JsonElement and ride into COM. The LacerteSessionManager.cs:679 comment explicitly states the SDK does not validate detail-row shape, which is the project's own justification for client-side validation being load-bearing (DetailsTools.cs:18-21 reiterates this). SimulationStore has an ExceedsMax path but only enforces ClientID's 8-char cap — no other length gating exists, and the FieldEntry.MaxLength schema field is unpopulated across every base/*.json map (confirmed via grep), so the auditor's suggestion to "look up SDK column widths" is currently unrealizable. The control-character / type-whitelist parts are trivially actionable in sim with pure CLR string ops; tests follow the existing ValidateDetailWrite pattern (no Windows/SDK install needed).
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Two concrete changes, both sim-only:

1) In DetailsTools.ValidateDetailWrite, extend the signature to include the remaining strings and add a single shared `EnsureSafeText(field, value, maxLen)` helper that throws SyntheticStatusCodes.DetailWriteInvalid when: (a) length exceeds a conservative blanket cap (suggest 255 for Description, 50 for Prefix/Suffix/Source/CityAbbr/ImportSrc — matches the DBF column families common in the spec), or (b) the string contains any char in [\\x00-\\x08, \\x0B, \\x0C, \\x0E-\\x1F, \\x7F] (allow \\t \\n \\r). Apply to series/code/prefix/suffix/source/cityAbbr/importSrc/description. Skip the access-map MaxLength lookup — that data isn't populated yet (would be a follow-up when the spec-mining pass lands).

2) Add a private `NormalizeFieldWriteValue(object? value)` in LacerteSessionManager.WriteField (called before BuildPayload, before the access-map gate, so the rejection is logged with the same shape as other client-side rejects). Whitelist CLR types: null, string, bool, sbyte/byte/short/ushort/int/uint/long/ulong, float/double/decimal, DateTime, and JsonElement only when its ValueKind is String/Number/True/False/Null (extract to the underlying primitive). Reject Array/Object JsonElement with SyntheticStatusCodes.FieldWriteInvalid (or a new 9009 if there isn't one) carrying {field, clrType}. For string values, apply the same control-char and 255-char cap from step 1.

Cover with tests in DetailsToolsTests (control-char in Description rejected; 256-char Description rejected; oversize Prefix rejected) and FieldWriteToolsTests (array value rejected; embedded \\x00 in string value rejected; bare double accepted). All run off-Windows in sim mode.

title: Collapse FieldWriteTools + UpdateReturnTools into shared base/helper
description: LacerteFieldWrite and LacerteUpdateReturn are near-identical: same parameter list, same delegation to _session.WriteField(...), same response shape (UpdateReturnTools adds api='UpdateTaxReturn'). The session manager already year-routes internally, so the two tool surfaces are mostly documentation. Tool body is duplicated almost verbatim across the two files.
recommendation: Extract a private helper (or have UpdateReturnTools delegate to a shared FieldWriteTools.WriteFieldCore(...) static) so the response-shape, parameter forwarding, and StatusCodes.GetStatusInfo lookup live in one place. Both tools can keep their distinct [McpServerTool] attributes for model-clarity; only the implementation gets DRY'd.
rationale: Any change to the response shape (e.g. adding 'severity' or a 'changedAt' timestamp) currently requires editing both files. The duplication is silent: nothing alerts when one drifts from the other.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading both files. FieldWriteTools.LacerteFieldWrite (lines 41-68) and UpdateReturnTools.LacerteUpdateReturn (lines 43-71) are structurally identical: same 8-parameter signature, same WrapToolHandler.Run wrapper, same _session.WriteField call with identical argument order, same StatusCodes.GetStatusInfo lookup, same anonymous response object (UpdateReturnTools only appends api='UpdateTaxReturn'). The XML doc comments on both files explicitly state both funnel through the same session chokepoint, confirming the duplication is intentional surface-only — meaning the body genuinely should be DRY'd. Drift risk is real and silent: adding any response field (severity, changedAt, idempotencyReplay flag) currently requires synchronized edits to two files with no compiler enforcement. Fix is pure in-process C# refactor, no Lacerte/Windows wire-up, sim tests will catch regressions. Not bikeshedding — this is a textbook silent-coupling cleanup.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Extract a private static helper into a new internal class (e.g. `Tools/Internal/FieldWriteCore.cs`) exposing `static Task<string> Run(LacerteSessionManager session, int table, string clientNumber, string field, object? value, int? subClientID, string? stateAbbrev, bool dryRun, string? idempotencyKey, string? apiTag = null)`. The helper owns the WrapToolHandler.Run + WriteField call + StatusCodes lookup + response shape, conditionally adding `api = apiTag` when non-null. Each tool's [McpServerTool] method keeps its own [Description] attributes (model-facing surface differs intentionally — FieldWriteTools has richer per-param descriptions) and becomes a one-liner delegation: `FieldWriteCore.Run(_session, table, ..., apiTag: null)` vs `apiTag: "UpdateTaxReturn"`. Verify by running the existing test suite (481 tests) — if any test asserts on the response shape, both tools' assertions should still pass unchanged.

title: Inline EnsureLive — it's a misleading one-liner that always-throws in Live
description: EnsureLive() is called in 5 read chokepoints (ListClients/ReadClient/ReadTable/ReadDetail/ReadEFStatus). Its body is just 'if (Mode == Live) throw BridgeUnavailable'. The name reads 'ensure we can talk to live' but the implementation 'reject if live' is the opposite — a code reader trying to understand the live-mode read path is misled. The other write chokepoints check '_bridge == null' directly without this helper, so the convention is inconsistent.
recommendation: Either (a) rename to RejectLiveReadsPendingOdbc() so the intent is explicit, or (b) inline it at the 5 call sites and add a one-line comment '// Live ODBC reads pending Phase 4 task #39'. Option (b) is cleaner because it removes the name-vs-behavior mismatch and matches the pattern the write paths already use.
rationale: EnsureLive is a temporary scaffold — when Phase 4 task #39 wires ODBC, the entire method disappears. Until then the name fights the behavior. The session manager already has the verbose '_bridge == null -> BridgeUnavailable' pattern in WriteField/WriteDetail/CreateClient/Register/CanUseNewApis (6 copies); EnsureLive isn't shared with those, so it's not even saving repetition.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed and actually worse than reported. LacerteSessionManager.EnsureLive() at line 880-888 has body `if (Mode == Live) throw BridgeUnavailable` — the name says "ensure live" but the behavior is "reject live." It's called at 397/426/457/517/538. The five surrounding write chokepoints (lines 176, 361, 616, 708, 797) use the verbose `if (_bridge == null) throw BridgeUnavailable` pattern directly, confirming the inconsistency claim. CRITICAL additional finding the auditor missed: `LacerteAccessClient.cs:258` has a *second* method also named `EnsureLive()` with the opposite (correct, intuitive) semantics — it throws when COM is NOT available. Two private methods, same project, same name, opposite meanings. This is a real readability/maintenance hazard for the upcoming Phase 4 ODBC wire-up, because whoever opens the session manager to wire reads will see two `EnsureLive` calls in unrelated files and trip on the contradiction. Both methods are private and only referenced internally (no test references), so renaming is zero-blast-radius. Pure sim-side refactor — no Windows/Lacerte install needed.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Rename `LacerteSessionManager.EnsureLive()` to `RejectLiveReadsPendingOdbc()` (option (a) from the original recommendation), NOT inline it. Reasons to prefer rename over inline: (1) it removes the name collision with the legitimately-named `LacerteAccessClient.EnsureLive()` which has opposite semantics — the collision is a worse trap than the inconsistency with write paths; (2) keeping a single named method documents the Phase 4 follow-up in one place, so when ODBC wire-up lands, the deleter only has to remove one method + 5 call-site lines; (3) inlining would scatter the same comment to 5 places. Optional bonus: the bridge's EnsureLive is fine as-is — the rename here resolves the naming clash one-sidedly. ~10-minute change, no test updates needed (method is private and untested by name).

title: CreateClient marks EmailID/FirstName/LastName optional vs spec required-set
description: Spec §4 (Create section): `lacerte_client_create — IClientList.SetDataPath → IClient (TaxType, ClientID ≤8 chars, EmailID, FirstName, LastName) → CreateClient.` REQUIREMENTS.md §Create echoes: `Create a new client (Individual, Corporate, etc.) with the minimum required fields (TaxType, ClientID ≤ 8 chars, EmailID, FirstName/LastName).` The tool declares firstName, lastName, and emailID with `string? = null` defaults, and CreateClientTools validates only ClientID + TaxType; LacerteSessionManager.CreateClient only enforces ClientID length and year ≥ 2018. A caller can omit all three name/email fields and the create still attempts to execute. Live SDK will likely reject (InValidClientName / LengthExceeded) but the failure surfaces late with a less actionable message than a synchronous validation gate.
recommendation: Either (a) make firstName, lastName, emailID required parameters (drop the `= null` defaults and validate non-empty in CreateClientTools.LacerteClientCreate) and mirror in CreateClientArgs, or (b) explicitly document in the [Description] strings and DECISIONS.md why they are optional in this MCP despite being required per spec. Option (a) matches spec literally and gives operators a clear preflight failure.
rationale: Spec text explicitly lists these in the `minimum required fields` set; tool surface diverges by treating them as optional with no compensating gate.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by direct read. Lacerte_MCP_Structure_Spec.md line 145 and REQUIREMENTS.md line 40 both explicitly enumerate FirstName, LastName, EmailID inside the "minimum required fields" set for lacerte_client_create. The tool surface (CreateClientTools.cs:65-67) declares all three as `string? = null` with `[Description("... Optional.")]`, and the validation chain (tool gate at lines 81-156, session at LacerteSessionManager.cs:775-784, sim at SimulationStore.cs:493-515) never enforces presence — the sim silently writes `args.FirstName ?? ""` into C1_1, C1_2, C1_3. The `CreateClientArgs` record (LacerteSessionManager.cs:1224-1229) carries the same nullable-with-default shape. DECISIONS.md has no entry justifying the deviation. So the divergence is real, the spec text is unambiguous, and a caller can legitimately omit all three and get a sim "success" or a live late-failure (InValidClientName / LengthExceeded) with a less actionable message. Fix is pure C# in three files (tool, session args record, sim store) plus a handful of new tests and an ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md line — fully in-session, no Lacerte/Windows required. Useful because (a) it restores spec parity (a stated boundary invariant: tools surface validated, structured errors), (b) the LLM-facing [Description] currently lies to the model ("Optional."), which causes worse tool-use behavior than the cost of accepting one more arg.
verdict.refinedRecommendation:
Apply Option (a) — make the three fields required end-to-end, with a focused diff:

1. `src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/CreateClientTools.cs`:
   - Drop the `= null` defaults on `firstName`, `lastName`, `emailID` and change the type from `string?` to `string`.
   - Rewrite the three `[Description]` strings to remove "Optional." and explain the spec requirement (e.g. "First name (individual) OR entity-name override. Required per spec — pass an empty string only if you have explicit live-SDK evidence the field is dispensable for this module.").
   - Add three validation gates BEFORE the `var args = new CreateClientArgs(...)` line, mirroring the existing pattern: throw `LacerteSDKError(StatusCodes.InValidClientName, {...})` with a `reason` naming the missing field, when `string.IsNullOrWhiteSpace(...)` is true for each.

2. `src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/LacerteSessionManager.cs` line 1224 — change `CreateClientArgs` to make `FirstName`, `LastName`, `EmailID` non-nullable positional params (drop defaults). This is a recompile, no runtime cost; callers inside the repo are only the two CreateClient tool sites, which already supply values after the new validation gate.

3. `src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/SimulationStore.cs` `SimulateCreateClient` — add a defense-in-depth gate after the TaxModuleMismatch step that returns `InValidClientName` if any of the three name/email fields are null-or-whitespace. Belt-and-braces against any future caller that bypasses the tool layer.

4. `ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md` §lacerte_client_create — add a bullet under "Client-side validation" listing the three new required-field gates and which status they throw.

5. Tests: add `CreateClientToolsTests` cases covering missing/whitespace `firstName`, `lastName`, `emailID` each producing `InValidClientName (24)` with the correct `reason`. Update any existing happy-path test that currently passes nulls.

6. `DECISIONS.md` — log a dated entry "2026-05-30 — CreateClient name/email fields enforced as required per spec §4 / REQUIREMENTS §Create" so the next contractor can see why the change happened.

Skip Option (b). The "optional" framing is already inconsistent with the spec and the [Description] strings actively misinform the LLM.

title: Tables 6 and 7 have no table-level write block; spec marks them Read only
description: Spec §2 access column for DATA6 = `Read only` and DATA7 = `Read only` (DATA5 is `Read only (non-global); some globals R/W`). The field-write tool accepts table 1..7 with the description `1=Client, 2=SubClient, 3=State, 4=StateSubClient, 5=Status, 6=Display, 7=Forms` — no table-level rejection. Per-field gating via the access map exists in theory but is bypassed for DATA6/DATA7 by passing `force:true` (and the map is empty anyway — see other finding). A spec-aligned MCP would refuse table=6 and table=7 writes up front with a structured 9001/FieldIsReadOnly or 9009/ContextNotSet message, regardless of access map contents.
recommendation: Add a table-number gate in FieldWriteTools.LacerteFieldWrite (and UpdateReturnTools.LacerteUpdateReturn) that rejects table ∈ {6, 7} with `LacerteSDKError(StatusCodes.ExposedForRead, { table, reason: "DATA6/DATA7 are read-only per spec" })`. For DATA5, leave the per-field map gate as the enforcement point since spec allows `some globals R/W`.
rationale: Cheap structural gate that aligns with spec's table-access column; prevents the model from constructing a write call that can never succeed.

verdict.reasoning: Spec §2 of Lacerte_MCP_Structure_Spec.md is unambiguous: DATA6 = "Read only", DATA7 = "Read only" at the table level (DATA5 is more nuanced: "Read only (non-global); some globals R/W"). Confirmed by reading C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Tools/FieldWriteTools.cs (line 42 advertises 1..7 with no constraint), UpdateReturnTools.cs (same), LacerteSessionManager.WriteField (lines 577-660, no table check), and SimulationStore.ApplySimFieldWrite (lines 295-352, accepts any table 1..7 if the field passes the access map). The finding has ONE factual error: it claims the per-field map "is bypassed for DATA6/DATA7 by passing force:true" — that is wrong. FieldWriteTools does not expose a force parameter and WriteField calls AssertWritable without force, so today every DATA6/DATA7 write would actually be refused by the 9012 UnknownFieldAccess path (since the base/*.json maps are all empty — confirmed 0 hits for table 6/7). Despite that misread, the core spec-compliance point is real: an empty map happens to gate writes today, but the moment the access map is populated with any DATA6/DATA7 fields (or someone wires force:true upstream) the table-level invariant disappears. A 4-line table-level gate makes the spec invariant load-bearing in code, independent of map state, and gives the model a far clearer rejection (table-level "DATA6/DATA7 are read-only per spec") than a per-field 9012/Unknown. Cheap, sim-only, aligns with ARCHITECTURE invariant "access map consulted on every write" by adding a coarser pre-check, and easy to add a test for. Not bikeshedding — it's a structural defense-in-depth gate on a non-negotiable spec rule.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add a table-number gate in LacerteSessionManager.WriteField (the chokepoint — preferred over duplicating in both FieldWriteTools and UpdateReturnTools) immediately after RejectIfReadOnly and before the idempotency check. Throw `new LacerteSDKError(StatusCodes.ExposedForRead, new Dictionary<string,object?>{{"table", table}, {"reason", "DATA" + table + " is read-only per spec §2 (Display/Forms tables are not writable through the SDK)."}})` for table ∈ {6,7}. Leave DATA5 to per-field gating (spec allows some globals R/W). Also add the symmetric guard to SimulationStore.ApplySimFieldWrite (return StatusCodes.ExposedForRead directly so the sim wire path stays observationally identical without throwing). Add tests in WriteParityTests covering: (a) table=6 rejected with ExposedForRead in both sim and live-stub paths, (b) table=7 same, (c) table=5 still passes through per-field gate. Make sure FieldWriteTools' [Description] for the table parameter mentions "1..5 writable; 6 (Display) and 7 (Forms) are read-only" so the model never tries.

title: Detail-file Series column typed string in record vs numeric in SQL filter
description: Spec §2 says detail-file columns are `Series, Prefix, Code, Suffix, StateAbbr, CityAbbr, Source, TSJ, ImportSrc, Amount, Description` with `Series ≈ Lacerte input screen, Code ≈ input field`. SqlTemplates.DetailBySeries treats Series as a numeric (`where Series = {series}` with int parameter) and DetailByCode treats Code as numeric (`where Code = {code}` with int). But the sim record (SimulationStore.cs line 46-57) types both as `string` — and seed data (SeedData.cs lines 104, 110, etc.) uses string values like `"Wages"`, `"Int"`, `"Div"` for Series. DetailsTools.LacerteDetailWrite also takes `series` as a string and `code` as a numeric string. The live SQL template will silently fail to match sim seed data (`Series = 'Wages'` won't bind to a Series=11 integer column). The sim and the SQL disagree on the column type.
recommendation: Decide canonically: either (a) Series is integer per Lacerte schema reality — change DetailRow.Series to int, update seed data to use the documented numeric Series IDs (11=W-2, 12=Interest, etc.), and update the tool to take int; or (b) Series is string and the SQL template should quote it (`where Series = '{series}'`). The SDK docs treat Series as a numeric screen identifier, so (a) is the spec-aligned choice. Same audit on Code.
rationale: Sim/live wire-shape divergence: live SQL won't match what sim emits, breaking the two-mode parity invariant for detail-row reads.

verdict.reasoning: The divergence is real and confirmed by reading the files. SqlTemplates.cs lines 180-191 emit unquoted-integer WHERE clauses (`Series = {series}` with int param, same for Code). Research agent docs (docs/research/agents/03-odbc-dbf-access.md line 246, 341) confirm live wire shape is numeric (`Series = 11`, example payload `{Series: 11, Code: 200}`). Meanwhile sim DetailRow.Series and DetailRow.Code (SimulationStore.cs lines 47, 49) are typed `string`, and SeedData uses friendly strings like "Wages"/"Int"/"Div" with Code="1"/"2". DetailsTools.LacerteDetailWrite also takes Series as string with no numeric validation. Two important nuances: (1) DetailBySeries/DetailByCode are not currently called by any tool — LacerteDetailRead returns all rows unfiltered — so the live break is latent, not active; (2) the project already self-flags this as v1 tech debt (DetailsTools.cs line 23 comment: "v1 accepts any string — TODO: real per-module Series enum"). The finding correctly identifies a parity invariant violation that will bite the moment a Series-filtered read tool ships or anyone runs the SQL templates live. Fully sim-side fix, off-Windows actionable. Worth doing; not bikeshedding.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Adopt option (a) but stage it to preserve readability: (1) Change DetailRow.Series and DetailRow.Code from string to int in SimulationStore.cs. (2) In SeedData.cs add a static `SeriesIds` lookup (`Wages=11, Int=12, Div=13, Dep=14, Inc=20, State=30`) with a comment citing the Lacerte SDK Series ID table from spec §2, then rewrite seed rows as `new DetailRow(SeriesIds.Wages, "", 1, ...)` so the seed data stays human-readable but emits the numeric IDs live SQL expects. (3) Change DetailsTools.LacerteDetailWrite's `series` and `code` params from string to int; drop the `_rxNumeric` Code check (compiler enforces it); update [Description] attributes to document the Series-ID mapping. (4) Update the v1-string TODO comment in DetailsTools.cs line 23 to closed. (5) Refresh DetailsToolsTests + SimulationStoreTests + RoundTripTests assertions that compare against the old string values. Optionally expose a `LacerteDetailReadBySeries` tool now that the templates are wired correctly. Same audit applies to Code — same fix shape.

title: EditionDetection live-throws branch + cached-once invariant untested
description: EditionDetection.Probe (EditionDetection.cs:38-63) has 2 branches: bridge==null returns the sim sentinel, bridge!=null throws BridgeUnavailable. Only the null-bridge branch is exercised (indirectly via SessionStatus in LacerteSessionManagerTests.cs:390). The 'live bridge present → throws BridgeUnavailable with op + reason context' branch has no test. There's also no EditionDetectionTests.cs file at all. The one-shot probe caching in LacerteSessionManager.EnsureEditionProbed (LacerteSessionManager.cs:283-295) is asserted via Assert.Same(status.Edition, status2.Edition) but only for sim — there's no test that the cache survives a probe THROW (today an exception would set _edition=null and re-probe forever, hammering the bridge on every SessionStatus call).
recommendation: Add EditionDetectionTests.cs with: (1) Probe(null) returns the 3 sentinel constants; (2) Probe(non-null bridge) throws LacerteSDKError with SyntheticStatusCodes.BridgeUnavailable AND context['op']=='EditionDetection.Probe'. In LacerteSessionManagerTests.cs add: inject a fake bridge that throws on first call, call SessionStatus twice, assert the bridge is hit twice (documenting the re-probe-on-throw behavior — OR fix it to cache the failure too if that's preferred).
rationale: EditionDetection is the only late-bound COM probe in the session-status path. The throw branch is what every live call will hit until Phase 9 lands; untested means a regression to the error envelope shape would surface only on the Windows box. The 'cache survives throw' question is a real design ambiguity the test would force a decision on.

verdict.reasoning: Verified directly. EditionDetection.Probe (src/LacertMCP.Server/Bridge/EditionDetection.cs:38-63) has exactly the two branches the finding describes: null-bridge returns the three sim sentinels; non-null bridge unconditionally throws LacerteSDKError with SyntheticStatusCodes.BridgeUnavailable and context keys ["op"="EditionDetection.Probe", "reason"="..."]. Grep for "EditionDetection" in tests returns zero hits — no EditionDetectionTests.cs file exists. The only coverage is LacerteSessionManagerTests.SessionStatus_InSimMode_ExposesSimulatedEdition (line 390-406), which uses NewSimManager() — the null-bridge branch only. The cache-on-throw concern is also real: EnsureEditionProbed (line 283-295) assigns _edition only if Probe returns; if Probe throws inside the lock, _edition stays null. SessionStatus then swallows the throw (line 250-260) and returns Edition=null, but the next SessionStatus call will re-enter the lock and re-probe — so a persistent live failure hammers the bridge once per status call. The internal test-only ctor (line 141, `internal LacerteSessionManager(ILacerteBridge bridge, ...)`) accepts a fake bridge and forces Mode=Live, so a throwing fake is trivial to wire — no Windows or real SDK needed. SessionManagerBridgeWireupTests.cs already demonstrates this fake-bridge injection pattern. Fixable entirely in sim. Useful because (a) it pins the live-error envelope shape (op/reason) the operator will hit until Phase 9, and (b) it forces a design decision on cache-on-throw before live wire-up.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Add src/LacertMCP.Tests/Bridge/EditionDetectionTests.cs with three tests: (1) `Probe_NullBridge_ReturnsSimSentinels` — asserts the three EditionDetection.Simulated* constants come back unchanged; (2) `Probe_LiveBridge_ThrowsBridgeUnavailable` — passes a stub ILacerteBridge (any throwing or no-op impl), asserts `ex.StatusCode == SyntheticStatusCodes.BridgeUnavailable`, `ex.Context["op"]?.ToString() == "EditionDetection.Probe"`, and `ex.Context.ContainsKey("reason")`; (3) `EditionInfo_Ctor_RejectsNullStrings` (cheap — three ArgumentNullException assertions on the three positional params). In src/LacertMCP.Tests/Session/LacerteSessionManagerTests.cs add `SessionStatus_LiveProbeThrows_ReProbesEachCall` using the internal test ctor with a fake bridge whose Dispose just counts and a Probe stand-in that increments a counter via a throwing dispatched method — since Probe is static and dispatches on `bridge == null`, the fake just needs to be non-null. Call SessionStatus twice, assert Edition is null both times and document via comment that this re-probes (XFAIL-style) — OR, cleaner, decide to cache the failure: change EnsureEditionProbed to assign a sentinel "probe-failed" EditionInfo (or a separate `_editionProbeFailed = true` flag) in a try/catch, then add the test asserting the bridge is hit exactly once across N SessionStatus calls. Recommend the cache-on-throw fix since this is a process-lifetime probe and SessionStatus is called frequently. (Phase 9 can revisit once the real probe is wired.)

title: WireLog redaction misses arrays, nested objects, and whitespace-padded JSON
description: The _redactRegex only matches scalar values: "(?<key>SSN|EIN|BankAccountNumber|RoutingNumber)":("..."|number|true|false|null). It does NOT match: (a) array values — '"SSN":["123-45-6789"]' passes through verbatim with the SSN in plaintext; (b) object values — '"SSN":{"value":"123-45-6789"}' passes through; (c) the inner key in nested objects — if a DetailRow.Description happens to JSON-serialize as '{"SSN":"x"}' inside a Description field it's redacted, but if it serializes as an array it isn't. WireLogTests.cs covers only the flat-scalar happy path. The integration test (WireLogSessionIntegrationTests.cs:127) uses the same flat shape. CreateClientArgs.EmailID flows verbatim to the log (LacerteSessionManager.cs:789-790) — email isn't on the redaction list but operators may put SSN in firstName fields for testing; the regex won't catch that either.
recommendation: Either: (1) document the scalar-only contract explicitly + add a [Fact] proving arrays/objects are NOT redacted (so future maintainers don't assume coverage they don't have); OR (2) replace the regex with a JSON-walking redactor (System.Text.Json JsonNode + recursive key check) and add tests for array+nested+pretty-printed (whitespace-padded) JSON. Recommend option 2 — the security-leak risk is asymmetric and the WireLog enables only when LACERTE_DEBUG_WIRE=1 so perf isn't critical.
rationale: Per CLAUDE.md and ARCHITECTURE.md, WireLog redaction is explicitly the 'before-disk' control for SSN/EIN/Bank/Routing — i.e. a security boundary. A regex-based redactor that silently skips arrays is the textbook 'sanitization that gives operators false confidence' bug. With the wire log being the primary debugging artifact, an SSN landing in plaintext is a real disclosure risk.

verdict.reasoning: Verified by reading WireLog.cs lines 62-64. The regex alternation `(?:"[^"]*"|-?\d+(?:\.\d+)?|true|false|null)` literally has no branch for `[` or `{`, so `"SSN":["123-45-6789"]` and `"SSN":{"v":"123-45-6789"}` pass through verbatim. The XML doc on the regex (lines 36-37) makes the stronger claim that "arbitrary JSON shapes are covered" — that is false and a real false-confidence security bug for code documented as the "before-disk" sanitization boundary. Today's call sites (LacerteSessionManager logs scalar DetailRow + CreateClientArgs) don't actually expose arrays-of-SSNs, so the *current* leak surface is small; the value of fixing it is (a) the comment is misleading and (b) future logged shapes (batched writes, list-typed args) would silently leak. Fully in-session fixable — System.Text.Json.Nodes already ships in net48 via the existing System.Text.Json dependency, and the existing Redact()/WriteForTest test seams cover the change with zero Lacerte dependency. The finder's "email in firstName" tangent is speculative and should be dropped from the recommendation — that's an operator-process issue, not a redactor bug.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Replace the regex in WireLog.Redact with a JsonNode-walking redactor: parse the JSON; recursively descend through JsonObject/JsonArray; when a property name (case-insensitive) is SSN/EIN/BankAccountNumber/RoutingNumber, replace the entire subtree (scalar OR object OR array) with the string "***". On parse failure, fall back to the existing regex (the safe-net for malformed JSON the existing defensive catch can produce). Also: (a) correct the XML doc on _redactRegex which currently claims "arbitrary JSON shapes are covered" — that claim is what makes this a security-boundary bug rather than a comment nit; (b) add three [Fact]s to WireLogTests.cs proving redaction of array-valued, nested-object-valued, and pretty-printed (WriteIndented=true) shapes; (c) keep _redactRegex as the fallback for the malformed-JSON branch only. Scope is ~60 LOC + 3 tests, pure C#, no Windows/Lacerte dependency. Skip the operator-puts-SSN-in-firstName concern from the original finding — that's out of scope for the redactor.

title: MetadataTools calls Schema layer directly, skipping session manager
description: LacerteFieldAccessMap calls FieldAccessMapLoader.GetFieldAccess directly instead of routing through the session manager. The architecture table lists Schema as a layer that tools may read (the catalog), so this is borderline, but the tool also encodes its own char→friendly-name table (_moduleFileName) that duplicates Modules.cs. The probe grid (C{t}_0..C{t}_25) is a tool-side guess at field shape that arguably belongs in the schema layer.
recommendation: Add session.GetFieldAccessMap(module, table, year) (or move the probe loop onto FieldAccessMapLoader as EnumerateKnownFields(module, table, year)) and have the tool call that. Drop _moduleFileName in favor of Modules.GetByChar(...).Name for the friendly label.
rationale: Per the architecture table tools may consult the schema, but the probe grid is logic, not a catalog read — it belongs server-side so the access-map version evolves in one place.

verdict.reasoning: Mixed verdict. The "skipping session manager" part is a false positive: ARCHITECTURE.md §Module Boundaries explicitly designates Schema as a static catalog tools may read, and FieldAccessMapLoader is called statically from SessionManager, SimulationStore, CLI, and tests — adding a session.GetFieldAccessMap pass-through would be ceremony with no state to manage. However, the duplicated _moduleFileName dictionary is a real problem, and inspection turned up a sharper concrete bug the finder hinted at but didn't name: MetadataTools returns moduleName="individual" (lowercase filename basename) while SessionTools.cs:220 returns moduleName="Individual" (Modules.GetByChar(...).Name) for the exact same field. Two tools, one field name, two different casings — a real cross-tool inconsistency. ACCEPTANCE_CRITERIA.md §lacerte_field_access_map doesn't pin the casing, so aligning on Modules.Name is safe. The probe-grid relocation suggestion is bikeshedding — discovery enumeration over a static catalog isn't policy logic and "tools may consult the schema" covers it.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Drop the local _moduleFileName dictionary in MetadataTools.cs entirely. Replace lines 52-61 with `var moduleInfo = Modules.GetByChar(module); if (moduleInfo == null) throw new LacerteSDKError(StatusCodes.InValidClientName, new Dictionary<string,object?>{ ["module"] = module.ToString(), ["validModules"] = string.Join(",", Modules.All.Select(m => m.Char)) });` and replace line 123 with `moduleName = moduleInfo.Name`. This (a) removes the dup, (b) fixes the cross-tool inconsistency with SessionTools.cs:220 (both now return "Individual" not "individual"), and (c) eliminates the only Schema-internal coupling. Skip the session.GetFieldAccessMap pass-through (pure static, no state to manage) and skip moving the probe grid into the loader (discovery enumeration isn't access-policy logic; the current behavior is fine and is covered by existing tests). Update MetadataToolsTests if any assert on moduleName casing (a quick grep shows none do).

title: Inverted EnsureLive() name conflates 'no live wiring' with 'is live mode'
description: The helper is named EnsureLive() but its body throws BridgeUnavailable when Mode == Live. Reading the call sites suggests the intent was 'we're past the sim-fallthrough, so confirm we have a real wire'. The negated semantics make every read-path call site harder to audit and contradict the comment 'Sim path is always live'.
recommendation: Rename to ThrowIfLiveReadsUnwired() or RequireSimMode() and document explicitly that 'this gate exists because live reads are not yet wired'. Update all five call sites in one sweep.
rationale: Architecture audits should not have to read the body of every helper to know which way the boolean flows. The current name actively misleads.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at C:/Users/VR/Projects/LacertMCP/src/LacertMCP.Server/Session/LacerteSessionManager.cs:880-888. The helper truly is inverted: `EnsureLive()` throws `BridgeUnavailable` precisely when `Mode == SessionMode.Live`, and falls through for sim. The internal comment "Sim path is always live" overloads the word "live" (operational-store-present vs SessionMode.Live), which is exactly the cognitive trap an architecture auditor hits. The five call sites (lines 397, 426, 457, 517, 538) all immediately call RequireSimModule afterward, confirming the call-site intent is "this read path only supports sim today." Pure rename + comment fix, no Windows/SDK dependency, contained to one file. Low severity but the cost is also low and the audit value is real (boundary invariants are non-negotiable per ARCHITECTURE.md, and helpers that fight their own names erode that audit-ability).
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Rename `EnsureLive()` to `ThrowIfLiveUnwired()` and update all five call sites in one sweep. Replace the internal comment with: `// Read paths are sim-only until Phase 9 wires the bridge + ODBC. Sim falls through; live throws BridgeUnavailable.` This phrasing (a) makes the boolean direction obvious from the name alone, (b) survives the Phase 9 cut-over without another rename (the method body simply becomes a no-op or gets deleted once live reads are wired, and the call-site call becomes harmless), and (c) avoids the alternative `RequireSimMode()` which would itself need renaming once both modes are valid. Keep the helper private and the signature `void`.

title: Session manager's _odbc field is `object? = null` placeholder, not typed
description: The session manager declares `private readonly object? _odbc = null;` with a 'Phase 4 task #39 still pending wire-up' comment. The comment claims the field exists for ODBC dispatch, but its type is untyped object?, never assigned, and never read anywhere in the file. This is dead weight that signals incomplete architecture in a class otherwise described as 'all originally-planned tasks done'.
recommendation: Either remove the field entirely (and the comment) or replace it with a typed `LacerteDsnReader? _odbc` field that is constructed in the Live-mode constructor branch and consumed by the read chokepoints once Stream A wires them. Pair this with the EnsureLive rename so the unwired state is honest.
rationale: Untyped placeholder fields in a chokepoint class invite future contributors to treat them as 'safe to ignore' and let real divergence between sim and live persist.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading LacerteSessionManager.cs line 60. The field `private readonly object? _odbc = null;` is genuinely untyped, never assigned anywhere (only initialized to null at declaration), and only "read" in Dispose() at line 1215 where `(_odbc as IDisposable)?.Dispose()` is a guaranteed no-op since the cast target is permanently null. A real `LacerteDsnReader` class exists at src/LacertMCP.Server/Odbc/LacerteDsnReader.cs and is the obvious type the field should hold. This is dead weight that does signal incomplete architecture — by contrast `_bridge` next to it is typed `ILacerteBridge?` and actually constructed in the live branch. The fix is a pure off-Windows code change (no Lacerte install needed). The recommendation's "EnsureLive rename" tangent is scope creep and should be dropped — that's a separate finding's territory.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Replace `private readonly object? _odbc = null;   // Phase 4 task #39 still pending wire-up.` with a typed `private LacerteDsnReader? _odbc;` field. In the Live constructor branch, leave it null (do NOT eagerly construct — the connection string isn't available until SetContext supplies dataPath, and constructing a reader here would couple session ctor to ODBC config). Add a `// Phase 4 task #39 — constructed lazily on first ODBC read with the active DSN connection string; null until then.` comment to document the lazy-wire intent. The Dispose() cast `(_odbc as IDisposable)?.Dispose()` can then become a direct `_odbc?.Dispose()`. This preserves the architectural placeholder honestly (typed, nullable, documented as lazy) without pretending the wire-up is done. Do NOT attempt to actually wire reads through it — that's Stream A / Phase 4 work and requires the live ODBC path.

title: EnsureEditionProbed re-probes on every call when the live probe throws
description: The docstring promises 'one-shot edition probe ... never re-probed for the lifetime of the process'. But the implementation only caches on success: when EditionDetection.Probe throws (currently always in live mode — see EditionDetection.cs:57), `_edition` stays null, the lock releases, and the next SessionStatus() call enters the lock and reprobes. Each SessionStatus() call therefore drives a fresh failing probe through the bridge. Combined with the swallowing `catch (Exception)` in SessionStatus() (line 255), the symptom is hidden: tools see edition=null on every status read with no log of the repeated probe failure.
recommendation: Cache the failure sentinel (e.g. assign `_edition = EditionInfo.Unavailable` or a Lazy<EditionInfo?> that captures the exception) so repeated probes don't happen. At minimum log the first failure at warning level via WireLog so operators see why edition is null.
rationale: Not a correctness bug per se but it breaks the one-shot caching contract documented in the docstring and could repeatedly hit a slow/hanging COM call. Once Phase 9 wires the real edition probe, this latent bug surfaces as SessionStatus() taking unbounded time on every call when the bridge is degraded.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading both files. EnsureEditionProbed (LacerteSessionManager.cs:283-295) assigns _edition only on a successful Probe() return; an exception leaves _edition null inside the lock, so the next SessionStatus() re-enters the lock and re-probes. EditionDetection.Probe (Bridge/EditionDetection.cs:57) unconditionally throws BridgeUnavailable in live mode today (Phase 9 stub). The catch(Exception) at SessionStatus line 255 silently coerces to null, hiding the symptom. Docstring at 275-282 explicitly promises one-shot caching, so the contract is broken. Latent today (sim always succeeds; live edition path isn't operator-exercised yet), but lights up the moment Phase 9 wires real COM probes — a hanging/slow COM call would then hit on every status read. Fully fixable in sim with a fake throwing bridge in a unit test. Note: CanUseNewApis has the same shape (ConcurrentDictionary.GetOrAdd doesn't cache exceptions), but its docstring doesn't promise one-shot caching the same way, and live failures there propagate rather than being swallowed — so this finding is genuinely scoped to the edition probe.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Two-part fix, both sim-testable: (1) Cache the attempt, not just success — wrap the probe in try/catch inside EnsureEditionProbed and on failure assign _edition = new EditionInfo("Unavailable", "Unavailable", "Unavailable") (or add a private bool _editionProbed sentinel) so subsequent SessionStatus calls return the cached unavailable triple without re-entering Probe(). (2) Log the first failure once via WireLog.RecordSync (or a direct WireLog write) at warning level with op="EditionDetection.Probe" so operators see why edition is "Unavailable" instead of silent null. Add a unit test using a fake ILacerteBridge whose ComInstance throws, asserting Probe is invoked exactly once across N SessionStatus calls. Leave the SessionStatus catch in place as defense-in-depth but it should now be unreachable for this path.

title: App.config carries no configurable settings — env-only configuration
description: App.config is currently 14 lines of pure runtime-shim (`useLegacyV2RuntimeActivationPolicy` + `supportedRuntime v4.0/v4.6`) — load-bearing per the comment. All configuration (DSN name, default tax year, datapath, log path) flows through environment variables only. This is fine and matches MCP convention (env in the host's mcpServers JSON), but it does mean: (1) no fallback when env is missing for an operator who wants persistent local settings; (2) no `lacerte-mcp config` command to inspect/set defaults; (3) `LACERTE_DSN=LacerteDSII` is documented as the default but the literal `LacerteDSIIDriver` is hardcoded in `ConnectionStringBuilder.cs:65` rather than read from config.
recommendation: Either (a) document explicitly in README/ARCHITECTURE that 'all configuration is environment-only — App.config holds only the runtime shim,' so future contributors know not to add appSettings here; or (b) add an optional <appSettings> section to App.config that env vars override at startup — gives operators a persistent settings file separate from the MCP host's JSON. Either way, surface the DSN-name vs driver-name distinction in the docs (currently the env var `LACERTE_DSN` is documented as the DSN, but the code uses a different driver-name literal).
rationale: The driver-name vs DSN-name confusion in the code+docs is a real bug magnet (the operator may set LACERTE_DSN expecting it to propagate to ConnectionStringBuilder and find it doesn't). Either pick env-only and document it loudly, or close the loop with an actual config file.

verdict.reasoning: App.config is indeed only a runtime shim as described. More importantly, the finding's core claim is verifiable: `LACERTE_DSN` is documented in README.md:78, ARCHITECTURE.md:175, and .env.example:20 as an operator-tunable env var defaulting to `LacerteDSII`, but a grep of all .cs files shows ZERO reads of `LACERTE_DSN` anywhere. It is dead config. Meanwhile `ConnectionStringBuilder.cs:65` hardcodes `Driver={LacerteDSIIDriver}` (a different identifier — the ODBC driver name, not the DSN name) and the only place the literal `LacerteDSII` (DSN) appears is in `DoctorCommand.cs:256-257` as a hardcoded registry probe. So an operator setting `LACERTE_DSN=MyCustomDsn` would (a) silently have no effect on the live connection (it's DSN-less anyway, built from driver+datapath+module+year) and (b) have their doctor still probing only for the literal `LacerteDSII`. That is a real documentation-vs-code drift bug. Fixable in-session without Windows: either delete the env var from README/ARCHITECTURE/.env.example (since ConnectionStringBuilder is intentionally DSN-less per `03-odbc-dbf-access.md`), or wire it through DoctorCommand's registry probe so the documented default is actually honored.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Drop `LACERTE_DSN` from README.md (line 78), ARCHITECTURE.md (line 175), and .env.example (line 20) — the production ODBC path is intentionally DSN-less (driver + datapath + module + year), confirmed by `docs/research/agents/03-odbc-dbf-access.md` §2 and the fact that no .cs file reads the var. Replace those rows with a short note: "ODBC connections are DSN-less; the `LacerteDSII` DSN is only probed by `lacerte-mcp doctor` as an install-sanity check." Optionally also make DoctorCommand's hardcoded DSN string (`DoctorCommand.cs:256-257, 273`) read from an env var if you want operators with custom DSN names to still get a green doctor probe — but the env var should be honored everywhere it's documented, or removed everywhere. Leave App.config alone; the comment correctly explains why it holds only the runtime shim.

title: AssertWritable allocates a new map-key string on every access-map lookup
description: GetFieldAccess fires on every write chokepoint (WriteField → AssertWritable → GetFieldAccess). Line 84 builds `"C" + table.ToString() + "_0"` and compares with ==; line 86 builds `module + "|" + table.ToString() + "|" + field` as the map lookup key. Each call allocates 2-3 strings + boxes the int via table.ToString(). On a 1000-field e-file write loop that's ~3000 transient strings just to gate the writes — small per call but on the GC-sensitive hot path the brief asked about.
recommendation: (a) For the universal C{table}_0 rule, compare via field.Length and per-character check instead of allocating, OR cache a static int->string array for table 1..7. (b) For the map key, switch the access-map dictionaries to be keyed by `(char module, int table, string field)` ValueTuple from the start (loader can build the composite key once at load time). That removes the per-call concat. Bonus: ValueTuple<char,int,string> hashes faster than the composite string anyway.
rationale: Not a single-call killer, but the access map is consulted on every single write per Boundary Invariant #6 — it's the closest thing this codebase has to an inner loop on the write path.

verdict.reasoning: Verified at C:\Users\VR\Projects\LacertMCP\src\LacertMCP.Server\Schema\FieldAccessMapLoader.cs lines 84 and 86. Both allocate strings on every GetFieldAccess call: line 84 builds the universal-rule comparison string and line 86 builds the composite map-lookup key, each via `+ table.ToString() +` (also boxes the int even though ToString returns a string, the concatenation forces extra allocations). AssertWritable is wired into WriteField (LacerteSessionManager.cs:595) and is also looped over by MetadataTools (lines 99/115) and the FieldAccessDumper utility, so it is a true batch caller. Fix is sim-only, pure-C# in Schema/, no Windows/Lacerte SDK dependency. The "1000-field write loop" perf claim is forward-looking — the base JSON shards are currently nearly empty `{}` so today's call counts are small — but the structural inefficiency is real and trivially cheap to fix now before the maps fill in. Recommendation (a) is clearly safe; (b) is correct but breaks ~4 test files that reflect into `_moduleCache` as `ConcurrentDictionary<char, IReadOnlyDictionary<string, FieldEntry>>`, so it should be scoped carefully or deferred.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Two-step fix, smallest-blast-radius first: (1) Universal-rule check on line 84: replace the concat-and-equals with an allocation-free comparison — `IsClientNumberField(field, table)` that checks `field.Length == (table < 10 ? 4 : 5)`, `field[0] == 'C'`, last two chars are `_0`, and middle chars parse to the table int (or simpler: precompute a `static readonly string[] _clientNumKeys = { "C0_0", "C1_0", ..., "C9_0" }` indexed by table for the common 0-9 range, fall back to concat for >9). (2) Composite key on line 86: introduce a `static readonly string[] _tableStrings` for tables 0-19 (or the actual SDK range) to skip the per-call `table.ToString()` and reuse interned strings; then `string.Concat(module.ToString(), "|", _tableStrings[table], "|", field)`. This preserves the existing `Dictionary<string, FieldEntry>` shape so the 4 test helpers that reflect into `_moduleCache` (SessionManagerBridgeWireupTests.cs:59, AccessMapTestFixture.cs:78-79, SessionManagerAutoReconnectTests.cs:37, WireLogSessionIntegrationTests.cs:47) keep working. Defer the ValueTuple key refactor — it's a larger change with test-helper churn and the string-keyed path with cached table-string lookup captures most of the win. Add a micro-benchmark test asserting no allocation in the universal-rule fast path (via `GC.GetAllocatedBytesForCurrentThread()` delta or similar) so the optimization doesn't silently regress.

title: Idempotency key compared with String.Equals — timing oracle when key is sensitive
description: TryReplayIdempotent looks up the key in a ConcurrentDictionary and compares PayloadFingerprint with the standard String.Equals (line 1136), which short-circuits on the first byte mismatch. If an attacker can submit speculative idempotencyKey+payload pairs and measure response timing, they can in principle learn a victim's fingerprint byte-by-byte and then mount IdempotencyConflict-as-oracle. The risk is low because (a) the fingerprint is SHA-256 of the payload, not a secret, (b) MCP isn't multi-tenant, and (c) timing over an MCP stdio pipe is noisy — but the same idempotency cache is also a cross-session memory primitive that holds prior write results indefinitely (no TTL on _idempotencyCache).
recommendation: Add a TTL to entries (drop after e.g. 24h, matching the session lifetime) and a max cache size cap to bound memory. Use CryptographicOperations.FixedTimeEquals (net48 has it via NuGet; otherwise port the constant-time-compare loop) for the PayloadFingerprint comparison. Add a synthetic 9103 for 'idempotency cache eviction' when an entry expired so callers can distinguish replay-miss from never-stored.
rationale: The realistic threat is the unbounded-cache memory leak more than the timing oracle. Both are cheap to fix; the constant-time compare is a defense-in-depth that future-proofs against MCP-over-network transports.

verdict.reasoning: Confirmed by reading LacerteSessionManager.cs:1129-1156 and IdempotencyCacheEntry.cs. The cache is a `ConcurrentDictionary<string, IdempotencyCacheEntry>` with no TTL, no max-size cap, and no eviction path — entries accumulate for the life of the process. The entry already carries a `CreatedAt DateTimeOffset` field that is currently set but never read, so the TTL plumbing is half-built. The timing-oracle half of the finding is essentially a non-issue here: this is a single-operator stdio MCP (CLAUDE.md/README.md confirm), the fingerprint is a SHA-256 of the payload (not a secret), and stdio doesn't expose remote timing. But the unbounded-cache half is real and trivially fixable: a long-lived MCP session that does many writes will leak boxed result objects forever. Both fixes are pure in-process C# work — no Windows/Lacerte dependency, sim+live observationally identical (the cache lives at the session-manager layer above the mode split). The synthetic-code addition for "cache eviction" is over-spec'd — a never-stored key and an evicted-then-replayed key are observationally identical to a well-behaved caller and adding a new code for it just expands surface area.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Fix the unbounded-cache leak; skip the constant-time-compare and the new synthetic code. Concretely: (1) Add `private const int MaxIdempotencyEntries = 1024;` and `private static readonly TimeSpan IdempotencyTtl = TimeSpan.FromHours(24);` constants to LacerteSessionManager. (2) In `TryReplayIdempotent`, after `TryGetValue` returns true, check `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow - entry.CreatedAt > IdempotencyTtl`; if so, `TryRemove` and return false (treat as miss — caller re-executes, same observable behavior as a brand-new key). (3) In `StoreIdempotent`, when `_idempotencyCache.Count >= MaxIdempotencyEntries`, drop the oldest entry by `CreatedAt` (single LINQ scan over ~1k entries is fine). (4) Add one unit test in LacertMCP.Tests that stuffs >MaxIdempotencyEntries entries and asserts Count stays bounded, plus one that uses reflection or a test-only seam to backdate CreatedAt and asserts replay returns false. Leave the `String.Equals` comparison alone — adding FixedTimeEquals here is defense-in-depth against a network transport that doesn't exist and changes the semantic to byte-equality on what is currently a managed string (correctness-equivalent only if both sides are normalized base64), so it's net-negative churn until/unless the transport actually changes.

title: AppId leak via error contexts and CLI commands — partial masking inconsistent
description: SessionStatusSnapshot.AppId is correctly masked to '***' (LacerteSessionManager.cs:271), but the AppId leaks through several other channels: (1) RegisterCommand prints the full GUID to stdout (lines 56, 66, 72) — the rationale is 'save for backup' but the prompt also says it can be re-read from CredMan; (2) LoginCommand prints the full GUID on every login (line 52) for no operator benefit; (3) AppIdStore.CredWriteOrThrow leaks the credential Target+Account into the InvalidOperationException message (AppIdStore.cs:262-263) — if that exception bubbles to a wire log via WireLog the credential-store coordinates leak; (4) DoctorCommand prints first-8 chars (line 195) which is reasonable but inconsistent with StatusCommand's 'first 8 + masked' format. The bigger leak: CanUseNewApisProbe.cs accepts appId as a parameter then discards it (line 81), so callers think it's used but it's actually unused — a future change might wire it into a log.
recommendation: Remove the full-GUID prints from LoginCommand (the GUID isn't needed for a refresh) and gate the RegisterCommand print behind a --show-app-id flag to match the StatusCommand convention. Mask the Target in CredWriteOrThrow's error message. Add an XML doc warning on every parameter named 'appId' that it must never appear in wire-log args or error context. Add an integration test that registers, then asserts the AppId GUID does not appear anywhere in lacerte_session_status output, any tool error response, or any wire log line.
rationale: The AppId is the SDK's bearer credential — leaking it lets any process on the box re-register as this MCP. Masking it in one channel while echoing it elsewhere defeats the purpose. The CredWrite error message leak is the highest-risk vector because it's the only channel that surfaces inside a generic exception path.

verdict.reasoning: Partially real, partially overstated. CONFIRMED: LoginCommand.cs:52 prints the full GUID on every refresh with no operator benefit (the operator already has it from register-time backup; login just refreshes the ticket). RegisterCommand.cs:56 also reprints the full GUID on the re-use path, which is arguably unnecessary after first mint. REFUTED: (a) CredWriteOrThrow's exception leaking Target='lacerte-mcp' and Account='app-id' is not a meaningful leak — both are public constants already exposed as AppIdStore.CredentialTarget/CredentialAccount and printed by StatusCommand line 56; they're discovery coordinates, not secrets, and any process can also just call CredRead with the well-known target. (b) The 'wire log leak' framing is wrong — CredWriteOrThrow lives in the CLI assembly and is only invoked by `lacerte-mcp register`; it never runs inside the MCP server's wire-log path. (c) CanUseNewApisProbe's `_ = appId;` is intentional with an explicit comment ('Pass appId as a context tag for the wire log') — flagging it as a future-foot-gun is speculative. The new-mint print at line 72 is legitimate (the operator must see the GUID once to back it up since CredMan storage is opaque). The threat model is also weak: any process on the box can already read the GUID from CredMan or the fallback JSON file directly. Net: there is a small, real, easy-to-fix tightening here (LoginCommand's redundant print, and inconsistent masking conventions across status/doctor), but the recommended integration test asserting 'GUID never appears in any tool error response or any wire log line' is the high-value piece — that's a useful invariant test even if today's code is fine.
verdict.refinedRecommendation: Two narrow, sim-friendly changes: (1) In LoginCommand.cs:52, replace `AppID  : {existing.Value:D}` with a masked form matching StatusCommand's Mask() helper (first 8 + ****) — login doesn't need the full GUID and runs more often than register. Extract Mask() from StatusCommand into AppIdStore (or a small Cli/Util class) so DoctorCommand line 195 and LoginCommand can share one canonical masking convention. (2) Add a unit/integration test in LacertMCP.Tests that: registers a known AppID, captures stdout from LoginCommand.Run and StatusCommand.Run (default), captures a SessionStatusSnapshot.ToString(), and asserts the full GUID string does not appear in any of those outputs. Skip: don't gate RegisterCommand's new-mint print at line 72 — the operator legitimately needs to see it once for backup. Skip: the CredWriteOrThrow message change — Target/Account are public constants, not secrets. Skip: XML doc warnings on every `appId` parameter — too noisy for marginal value.

title: Remove dead ConnectionPool helper (never referenced)
description: ConnectionPool.GetOrCreate is defined but referenced by no production or test code (grep finds zero callers outside its own definition). The file header explains why no second-layer pool is needed and the factory is a 1-line wrapper around new LacerteDsnReader(connectionString).
